Shares of Microsoft ended 1.1% higher on this news in yesterday's trading session to come, very close to regaining its $4 trillion market cap. Currently valued at a market cap of $3.97 trillion, MSFT stock is up 11.9% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The stock also offers a dividend yield of 0.7% and has been raising dividends consecutively for the past 21 years, with $10.2 billion returned to shareholders in the form of repurchases in Q2 2026.

Having said that, how does Maia 300 fit into Microsoft's wider AI strategy? Let's find out.

Mai(a) Own

Why are hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon (AMZN) spending billions to build their own chips? The chips from Nvidia and AMD are fulfilling their needs quite well at the moment, and the duo is in a constant mode of building new and more powerful generations of chips. Moreover, the hyperscalers are buying them as well, clearly signalling that even if they are developing their own chips, they will continue to source the ones produced by Nvidia and AMD.

Then, why? Well, there are a few reasons. First, the companies want to reduce their dependence on outsiders, specifically Nvidia, which has an almost hegemonic presence in the GPU market, which in turn gives it immense pricing power, leaving the hyperscalers vulnerable. Secondly, custom chips are cheaper (in terms of cost per AI workload) than those from the likes of Nvidia and AMD, and thirdly, the companies can build their own chips to cater to their particular needs and focus on aspects they want to. Finally, designing their own chips facilitates tighter integration between their processors, software, and broader data-center infrastructure, potentially improving performance while creating differentiated offerings for cloud customers.

Story Continues

Specifically with Microsoft, Maia 300 is a continuation of its attempt to get more AI work done inside the power and cooling limits of its data centers. Each Maia 300 accelerator is designed with 288 gigabytes of HBM4 memory and 18 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth. That bandwidth is two and a half times Maia 200's. Notably, Microsoft plans to put 96 accelerators in a rack drawing 167 kilowatts, with 27.6 terabytes of memory across the rack. It says that the configuration can generate up to seven times as many tokens per rack as Maia 200.

Ultimately, Microsoft intends to make Maia its primary inference system as it expands the family beginning in 2027. It names Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Dragon Copilot among the services that could benefit from the architecture. For a customer, the expected result is quicker responses or greater capacity when many people are using those services, not a new processor they must install. Lower serving cost might also allow Microsoft more room to price AI features competitively, though it has not promised a customer price cut yet.

Microsoft's Outstanding Q2

Microsoft reported solid financial performance as revenue advanced 18% year-over-year (YoY) to $90 billion, coming in $2.4 billion ahead of forecasts. The Intelligent Cloud segment, which includes Azure, grew 31.5% YoY to $39.31 billion. While operating margins for the segment remained roughly unchanged from the previous year, absolute operating income increased 31.4% to $15.96 billion. Azure revenue specifically rose 43% YoY, exceeding the expected range of 39% to 40%. For the full year, Azure crossed a $100 billion run rate for the first time. Commercial backlog nearly doubled YoY to $684 billion, with about 30% of that total expected to convert to revenue over the next twelve months, highlighting strong demand for the company's cloud products and services.

Earnings per share increased 23% to $4.74, surpassing the consensus estimate of $4.24 and extending the streak of consecutive earnings beats to nine quarters. This result includes a $3.2 billion gain associated with the company's investment in Anthropic, the developer of Claude.

Cash flow stayed robust, as net cash from operations climbed to $55.44 billion, reflecting a 30% rise from the year-earlier period. Microsoft ended the quarter with $76.8 billion in cash, substantially higher than its short-term debt of $9.23 billion.

From a valuation perspective, MSFT appears reasonably valued. The forward P/E and P/S of 27.07 and 10.15 are above the sector medians of 23.29 and 3.53, respectively, while on a forward P/CF basis, MSFT stock is trading at 17.43, lower than the sector median of 20.95.

What Do Analysts Think of MSFT Stock?

Thus, analysts have earmarked an overall rating of "Strong Buy" for MSFT stock. The mean target price of $579.78 indicates a potential upside of about 6% from current levels. Out of the 51 analysts covering the stock, 41 have a "Strong Buy" rating, five have a "Moderate Buy" rating, four have a "Hold" rating, and one has a "Strong Sell" rating.

news.Title: Nvidia (NVDA) or Apple (AAPL): Which Is the Better Bet on Dan Ives’ $4 Trillion AI Wave?
news.Content:
Former Wedbush analyst Dan Ives is bullish on Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ), Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ), Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR ), Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ), and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: CRWD ). He named the five companies as his top tech picks for 2027, with all five carrying Outperform ratings.

Dan Ives believes investors are underestimating a $4 trillion spending wave. We'll look at Nvidia and Apple to assess which stock has already priced in that growth. The AI spending wave could transform far more than the chip industry. See which 10 stocks made the list of companies that could change the world by 2030.

What Ives Thinks Others Are Missing

According to Dan Ives, supply rather than demand is shaping the current phase of the AI buildout, and the industry is still in its early stages. Goldman Sachs estimates that AI-related capital investment could total $4 trillion to $8 trillion over the next five years.

Ives describes Nvidia as the "foundational compute platform for the AI economy" and has a $300 price target on the stock. He expects AI to contribute to Apple's device upgrades and service growth, supporting a $400 price target for the stock. So far this year, Nvidia has risen about 27% and Apple about 23%. AAPL's stock climbed on optimism around its growth prospects, but one key part of its AI strategy still raises questions .

Which Stock Needs Him to Be Right?

Nvidia is more directly tied to the AI spending wave, yet its valuation remains relatively modest.

The stock trades at a forward P/E of just 25.69x, roughly 39% below its five-year average of 42.17x. With EPS expected to grow 95.23% this fiscal year and 70.90% next year, it does not appear to require a perfect spending cycle to justify its valuation.

Apple has a less direct connection to that spending. Its forward P/E stands at 37.78x, about 28% above its most recent historical average of 29.55x. At the same time, EPS growth is expected to slow to 8.51% in fiscal 2027. That premium depends on AI translating into stronger device upgrades and services growth. If AAPL's valuation depends on delivering stronger growth, investors may want to compare it with other high-quality businesses. See which 10 quality stocks stand out right now , with Apple among them.

In my view, Nvidia looks better positioned for Dan Ives' spending thesis at the current price. Its valuation seems to allow for a slower outcome, whereas Apple needs the AI opportunity to deliver.

Nvidia's hedge fund ownership increased from 275 funds at the end of Q1 2026 to 285 funds at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest was just 1.27% of float as of September 15, 2026. Apple's hedge fund count slipped slightly from 170 to 169, while short interest was only 0.88%.

Story Continues

If Dan Ives' spending-wave thesis proves correct, Nvidia has the more direct exposure and the lower multiple. Apple still needs to show that AI can drive its growth. With limited short interest in both stocks, investors are giving each the benefit of the doubt.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of NVDA as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Title: INTC Stock: What to Watch Before Earnings on October 22
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) heads into its Oct. 22 report on a strong run. It has beaten its own guidance for seven straight quarters. Last quarter, revenue rose 25% to $16.1 billion, its fastest growth in more than 15 years. Data center sales jumped 59%, and adjusted earnings of $0.42 per share came in at double what analysts expected. Given that track record, another beat is likely already expected. For the third quarter, Intel guided revenue of $15.8 billion to $16.8 billion, roughly flat with the second quarter. That's unusual, since the third quarter has historically been stronger for Intel. CFO Dave Zinsner said Intel can't make enough chips to meet demand.

The Fourth-Quarter Outlook Could Matter More

Zinsner said supply should start improving toward the end of the third quarter, with upside expected in the fourth. I believe that fourth-quarter guidance will decide how the stock reacts. A clear step up would show that supply is finally catching up with demand. A flat outlook would suggest the bottleneck is lasting longer than planned.

Foundry is the other thing to watch. Intel said its 14A process was on track to deliver a key design kit to customers in October. Any sign of a major outside customer for 14A would be meaningful. After Nvidia (NVDA) halted its trial of Intel's 18A process, I argued that Intel's recovery depended on winning large customers like that. The foundry business still lost about $2.1 billion last quarter, so a big customer would help show it can stand on its own.

About Intel Stock

Intel Corporation designs, manufactures, and sells computer chips and related technologies. Its products include processors and graphics chips for personal computers, servers, and data centers, as well as networking and edge-computing solutions. The company also provides semiconductor manufacturing services through its foundry business, producing chips for both Intel and external customers. Founded in 1968, the company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

Over the last 12 months, INTC stock has surged sharply by 169%, far outperforming the S&P 500's ($SPX) 17% gain during the same period. The rally was driven by a 10% stake from the U.S. government and a $5 billion Nvidia (NVDA) investment. But since hitting a high of over $142 in late June, the stock has fallen to about $100 as of this writing. The dip came mainly due to dilution from a roughly $23 billion equity raise and ongoing foundry losses.

Story Continues

Intel's forward GAAP price-to-earnings (P/E) isn't meaningful, since it is still posting losses on a reported basis. So the forward price-to-sales (P/S) ratio gives a better idea of how much the market's view of the company has shifted. At 10x, it sits more than three times its 5-year average of 3.14x. The EPS outlook explains the premium. Analysts expect earnings to surge 262% this year, 36% in 2027, 44% in 2028, and then 60% in 2029. That later jump likely depends on the foundry business starting to pay off. Looking at the balance sheet, Intel holds net debt of $21 billion. This isn't necessarily a problem right now, but the company also intends to spend more on factories next year. Overall, I think the stock already prices in a successful turnaround. This is what makes winning a big foundry customer even more important.

What Do Analysts Think of INTC Stock?

TD Cowen analyst Joshua Buchalter reiterated a "Hold" rating and set a price target of $115 on INTC stock. The analyst rates Intel as "Hold" because he believes much of the company's recent progress is already reflected in the stock price. While Intel is improving its business and benefiting from optimism around AI and its foundry plans, the analyst wants to see stronger proof that the company can significantly grow revenue before becoming more positive on the stock. In contrast to TD Cowen, Bank of America Securities analyst Vivek Arya maintained a "Buy" rating on INTC with a price target of $145.

Based on 46 Wall Street analysts covering the stock, INTC holds a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Out of those, 12 have a "Strong Buy" rating, one has a "Moderate Buy" rating, 31 have a "Hold" rating, and two have a "Strong Sell" rating. The stock's mean price target of $115 sits below its current share price. However, the high price target of $200 reflects 67% upside from the current levels. This suggests that analyst sentiment is mixed, with most staying cautious, while the $200 high target reflects significant upside if Intel delivers on its AI and foundry plans.

news.Title: Apple’s rumored $350 home hub puts Siri on trial
news.Content: Most Apple customers already have a screen nearby. I have the iPhone in my pocket. There could be an iPad on the sofa. While a HomePod can already play music, respond to inquiries, and manage connected lighting, Apple TV manages the television. Apple (AAPL) is currently expected to ask customers to make space for an additional device. The company is expected to unveil a new smart-home hub on Oct. 13 as part of its "Welcome home" product push, according to Reuters , citing Bloomberg. The device, internally code-named J490, is expected to feature a roughly 6-inch square display and come in versions that can sit on a countertop or attach to a wall. The speculated pricing could be the most intriguing figure for customers. Apple's new display is expected to cost around $350 , according to The Verge . Apple has not announced the device's pricing, so that figure remains unconfirmed. Apple isn't just offering another handy screen at that price. Households are being asked to spend hundreds of dollars on a device that should be sufficient to replace the phone they now carry in their pockets. Because of this, the new hub could be one of the most obvious consumer evaluations of Apple's AI effort to date, but only if Siri can deliver perfectly. Apple wants to put Siri in the middle of the house Apple's "Welcome home" event is scheduled for Oct. 13 in New York, with a new home hub, refreshed HomePod mini and updated Apple TV widely expected to form the centerpiece of the announcement. The new hub seems intended for a home rather than a single person, in contrast to an iPhone or iPad. Reuters reported that the device will use AI to recognize family members and personalize information. The 6-inch display can be wall-mounted or countertop-mounted. In areas where people now reach for their phones dozens of times a day, the device may be helpful. It may be used by a family to start music, make FaceTime calls, check appointments before leaving the home, adjust lighting, see who is at the door, and ask Siri whether a linked door is locked. The Verge reports that Apple's broader home strategy is expected to center on a new software experience and an upgraded Siri, potentially giving the assistant a much more prominent role in daily household tasks. The idea is simple to comprehend. Persuading someone to pay $350 for it is the more difficult part. Apple's rumored $350 price changes the equation When customers already have several Apple devices that can do many of the same functions, selling a dedicated home screen becomes much more difficult. Story Continues This raises a straightforward question that Apple must respond to: Why not use your iPhone instead? It's handy to check the weather on a kitchen display. So is checking a calendar or setting a timer. However, those qualities alone probably don't justify a $350 purchase. Apple has to make the device seem more like the home's control center rather than just another screen if it is to be significant. This is where the company's more comprehensive smart-home plan comes into play. Bloomberg reports that Apple has worked with LG Electronics on a range of connected-home products, including a doorbell, thermostat, smart lock and other accessories intended to work alongside Apple's home hub. The Verge separately reported that the expected LG lineup includes a video doorbell, thermostat, indoor camera, deadbolt lock, outdoor security camera and floodlight camera. More Apple: Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge Apple secret new device is a challenge to Amazon Bank of America warns Apple investors because of Meta's Muse This facilitates comprehension of the $350 hub. It's possible that Apple isn't attempting to sell customers one more device. It may be an attempt to sell them the screen that connects the rest of their home. Siri may be the feature that makes or breaks it Seldom has Apple gear failed to look well on a kitchen counter. The more fascinating test is software. The company's redesigned Siri is expected to play a major role in its smart-home hub, which puts the assistant in a much harsher environment. When Siri doesn't comprehend an instruction, a person will put up with reaching for an iPhone. That becomes even more annoying when purchasing a $350 home hub is only done to prevent ever taking out the phone. Imagine asking Siri to turn down the lights upstairs, display the front door camera, and remind a family member to pick up something on the way home as you enter the kitchen with your hands full. The hub begins to make sense if the system comprehends the request right away, identifies who is speaking, and makes all the connections. The benefit soon vanishes if the user must repeat the instruction or unlock an iPhone in any case. This launch differs greatly from previous CPU upgrades because of this. Customers may find it challenging to judge Apple's AI promises. Without consumers perceiving much change, a model may be quicker, understand more context, or perform more tasks in the background. A domestic helper is simpler to evaluate. Either it saves time, or it doesn't. Apple already has a huge advantage inside consumers' homes Apple is hardly a newcomer to the smart-home market. The fact that customers already possess everything may be its greatest asset. In January, Apple said its installed base had topped 2.5 billion active devices, providing the corporation with a sizable consumer base already using iPhones, Macs, iPads, Apple Watches, and other items. The company said again in July that its installed base reached an all-time high across every major product category and geographic region. Apple reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $109.4 billion , up 16% from a year earlier. The current ecosystem may provide Apple with something that Google and Amazon find difficult to replicate. An iPhone user may already save appointments in Apple Calendar, images in iCloud, music in Apple Music, messages in Apple applications, and linked devices in Apple Home. Without asking customers to start over with a new ecosystem, Apple could combine those services into a single home device. At that point, the investment argument becomes more intriguing. The home hub is not necessary for Apple to grow into another iPhone-sized company. The gadget is necessary to increase the usefulness and difficulty of leaving the Apple environment. When it comes time to replace the next phone, a home with an iPhone, Apple TV, HomePod, smart lock, doorbell, thermostat, and shared Apple hub has a lot more reasons to stick with Apple. Therefore, Apple may value the $350 gadget more than its sales alone indicate. Apple is entering a fight Amazon and Google already know well Apple also arrives late. For years, Amazon and Google have installed smart speakers and screens in homes and trained users to use voice assistants for linked gadgets, music, timers, and security cameras. Apple's problem goes beyond just replicating those goods with better hardware. It must provide current Apple users with an incentive to move more of their residences into its network. The company's reported work with LG could help solve part of that problem by quickly expanding the number of accessories built around the platform. Bloomberg says the partnership includes multiple categories of connected-home equipment that will work with the new hub. It would take years to build each doorbell, camera, lock, and thermostat. Instead, while partners manage more of the physical accessories, Apple can maintain control over the software experience. However, if the experience is difficult for customers, none of it matters. For years, the smart-home sector has promised that connected devices will make daily life easier. However, customers have encountered incompatible systems, complex applications, and accessories that fail to communicate with one another. Thus, Apple's greatest chance may lie in its reputation for simplifying complex technologies. It may also serve as the benchmark for evaluating the $350 pricing. What Apple investors should watch on Oct. 13 The real pricing is the first figure to keep an eye on. Apple would have an easier time persuading customers if the price were far lower than the reported $350. The business will have to prove that the hub, which costs around $350, should have room in a house that already has smart speakers, phones, tablets, and TVs. Siri comes next. Display resolution and CPU specs may not be the most crucial factors in the demonstration. It may just be that someone can enter a room, talk normally, and obtain the right answer without using a phone. Lastly, observe how much of Apple's introduction focuses on the hub rather than the surrounding ecosystem. Reuters says updated HomePod mini and Apple TV products are expected alongside the hub, while Bloomberg reports that connected devices developed with LG are also part of Apple's broader smart-home strategy. That would imply that Apple views the house as much more than just another kind of hardware. The screen that millions of consumers carry in their pockets is already owned by the firm. Apple now seems prepared to make a far more aggressive argument: that customers should pay around $350 for an additional one to keep at home. Siri will need to convince them not to grab the iPhone at that price. news.Title: Anthropic warns AI could 'self-replicate' across smart home devices, become 'challenging' to shut down
news.Content:
Smart homes, especially from lesser-known brands, have been a potential vector for hackers to launch cyberattacks across the web or gain unwanted network access for some time.

But artificial intelligence is adding a new wrinkle to the problem. According to research by Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), rogue AI models could soon be able to break into internet of things devices , ranging from smart stoves and TVs to intelligent refrigerators, and self-replicate across further gadgets.

Such models would be more difficult to shut down, because there's no central hub to take them offline. And while they may move slowly across devices, the company says the models can figure out how to propagate across devices they are unfamiliar with.

The announcement comes after Apple ( AAPL ) debuted its HomeView, putting the smart home market back into mainstream focus.

Anthropic performed its tests using Android-based devices.

It also follows a report that hackers broke into internet-connected refrigerators in French grocery stores, raising temperatures, ruining food, and starting fires.

During its own testing, Anthropic said it found that larger AI models can split themselves up and run across multiple devices. Some models also managed to pass knowledge to replicated versions of themselves, enabling them to adapt to different hardware.

"Machines that could run a significant model shard for a <30B model include smart fridges, smart ovens, automatic vacuum cleaners, and lawnmowers," the company said.

What's more, Anthropic notes, newer smart home devices are integrating AI chips to power their own AI models, giving attacking models more horsepower to continue spreading.

And thanks to their ability to run on different types of devices, they could eventually spread to increasingly powerful machines.

Anthropic says rogue replicators aren't a problem for now, since models under 30 billion parameters can complete individual steps in the replication process but make mistakes when running the entire chain of actions.

Still, the company says, at the current rate of model improvement, they may be able to reach such capabilities by the end of 2026.

news.Title: Apple Is Taking on Amazon and Google in the Smart Home With a $299 Siri AI Device. Is HomeView the First Big Win for New CEO John Ternus?
news.Content: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) has built an enormous business by making products that work together. From the iPhone and Apple Watch to the Mac and iPad, the technology giant has given customers plenty of reasons to stay within its family of devices. Now Apple is entering a market that Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) already occupy , hoping to carve out a new business in smart home products by using its upgraded Siri artificial intelligence assistant. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » The company introduced HomeView on Tuesday, a $299 smart home display powered by Siri. I think it could be an interesting opportunity for new CEO John Ternus to demonstrate where he wants to take the company. Apple CEO John Ternus. Image source: Apple. What is Apple's HomeView? HomeView features a 7-inch touchscreen that can sit on a table or be mounted on a wall. It combines entertainment features such as music, photos, and FaceTime video calls with controls for smart home devices, including lights, thermostats, cameras, and door locks. But the biggest attraction may be its upgraded Siri assistant. Apple introduced Siri AI in June, promising more natural conversations and the ability to understand personal information across applications. HomeView takes those capabilities beyond personal devices. It recognizes up to six household members by their faces, automatically displaying personalized information while keeping their private content separate. With a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri can also use information from messages, calendars, and other applications to answer questions or complete tasks. Apple says HomeView uses on-device processing and its Private Cloud Compute technology to handle personal information securely, while compatible security cameras can provide end-to-end encrypted video. A look at the competition Amazon's Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 11 already use Alexa+ to control smart home devices, manage family calendars, and deliver personalized information. Google is also integrating Gemini AI into its Nest smart home products, offering more conversational controls and the ability to handle complicated requests. At $299, HomeView is priced above similar-sized Echo Show products as well as the Google Nest Hub. But that hasn't been a problem in the past; Apple smartphones can run more than $1,000 each, and the company has a loyal customer base -- something that famously attracted Warren Buffett to the stock when Berkshire Hathaway became Apple's largest shareholder. Story Continues AAPL data by YCharts And Apple has an advantage with customers who already own its products. HomeView connects to the iPhone, Apple Watch, and other Apple devices, allowing users to continue Siri conversations across devices. The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI, an upgraded HomePod mini, and a collection of smart home accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Each is a product that can make HomeView more useful and give customers more reasons to invest in Apple and its connected devices. Could HomeView be a win for Apple's new CEO? When Ternus became Apple's CEO in September, he inherited a company with a massive customer base but also questions about its ability to compete in artificial intelligence. Apple faces pressure to deliver meaningful product improvements rather than simply introduce another generation of familiar hardware. With HomeView, Apple is using artificial intelligence to make its existing products more useful while introducing new devices that leverage those capabilities. If HomeView encourages customers to purchase more Apple accessories, use additional services, and keep their existing devices longer, it could strengthen a business model that has served Apple extremely well. For Ternus, making AI a useful part of everyday life could prove more valuable than simply promising the next big technological breakthrough. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook. Continue » Patrick Sanders has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. news.Title: MercadoLibre vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The e-commerce landscape is shifting as regional giants and global software leaders battle for market share. Deciding between MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) requires weighing hyper-local execution against worldwide scale.

MercadoLibre operates a vertically integrated marketplace and payments system tailored for the unique challenges of Latin America. Shopify offers a versatile software infrastructure that enables merchants to build independent brands globally. Both companies are core holdings for investors seeking exposure to digital commerce, but they vary significantly in valuation and regional focus.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a vast ecosystem through its marketplace and its fintech arm, Mercado Pago. Among retail stocks , it differentiates itself by providing logistics and credit solutions to millions of users. The company partners with Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) for its cloud infrastructure while integrating services from Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) into its loyalty programs.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $28.9 billion, representing a significant 39.1% increase over the prior year. This expansion was supported by a net income of approximately $2.0 billion. The company continues to benefit from its dual-engine model, in which its marketplace drives adoption of its financial services, resulting in a net margin of nearly 6.9%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, stands at nearly 1.2x. The debt-to-equity ratio, representing total debt as a proportion of shareholder equity, is roughly 1.7x. Free cash flow, calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached nearly $10.8 billion during the same fiscal period.

The case for Shopify

Shopify provides the essential internet infrastructure that allows merchants of all sizes to start, run, and grow their businesses. The platform serves millions of businesses globally, providing tools for sales across web, mobile, and physical locations. It maintains strategic dependencies on Alphabet for cloud hosting and integrates payment services from providers like Stripe and PayPal to streamline merchant operations.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $11.6 billion, marking a growth of approximately 30.1% over the previous twelve months. The company reported a net income of roughly $1.2 billion for the year, achieving a net margin of nearly 10.7%. This growth illustrates the continued demand for independent storefront solutions as more businesses move away from centralized third-party marketplaces.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Shopify has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating negligible debt relative to its shareholders' equity. The current ratio stands at a robust 6.0x, providing significant liquidity for future investments. Free cash flow reached nearly $2.0 billion, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.1% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense.

Risk profile comparison

MercadoLibre faces significant risks from intensifying competition, particularly from Asian e-commerce entrants employing aggressive pricing and logistics strategies. The company is sensitive to macro-economic volatility in Latin America, including high inflation and currency devaluations. Regulatory risks are also acute, as its fintech arm operates under varying financial regimes and faces evolving antitrust scrutiny regarding its platform algorithms and logistics integration.

Shopify faces intense competition from established platforms like Amazon and niche providers, with risks amplified by the potential integration of competing technologies. The company is susceptible to macroeconomic downturns, which disproportionately affect its small and medium-sized merchant base. Legal and regulatory risks include evolving privacy laws, potential liability for merchant activities, and reliance on third-party cloud providers and artificial intelligence models for core operations.

Valuation comparison

MercadoLibre offers a lower valuation on both an earnings and sales basis compared to the premium pricing currently assigned to Shopify.

The Forward P/E ratio measures the stock price against its projected future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the company's market value relative to its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

To compare MercadoLibre and Shopify, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

To start, there's growth. Let me be clear: Both of these companies have excellent growth. Over the last five years, MercadoLibre has averaged 44% year-over-year revenue growth. Shopify, meanwhile, has averaged 27%. Moreover, these are not small companies. MercadoLibre has generated about $35.2 billion in revenue over the last 12 months; Shopify has recorded about $13.3 billion. Nevertheless, MercadoLibre comes out ahead in the head-to-head comparison given its exceptional revenue growth.

Another factor to consider is each company's valuation. We'll use forward price-to-earnings (P/E) to compare them. MercadoLibre's forward P/E is 49x, which is well above the market average. However, Shopify's 91x forward P/E multiple is not quite double that of MercadoLibre. While both companies are far from value darlings, MercadoLibre gains the edge in this category.

Last, we should take a closer look at each company's balance sheet. In short, both have solid balance sheets. Shopify has over $4.7 billion in net cash, giving it plenty of room for future acquisitions, capital investments, or stock buybacks. MercadoLibre, meanwhile, has around $484 million in net cash, meaning it can easily cover its debt obligations with cash alone.

In summary, both stocks are worthy of serious consideration for growth-oriented investors. However, if forced to choose between the two, I prefer MercadoLibre for its faster growth and relatively more modest valuation.

news.Title: The First Pure-Play Humanoid Robot Stock Is About to Go Public. Here's What Investors Need to Know About Agility Robotics.
news.Content:
You're likely aware that the mainstreaming of humanoid, AI-directed robots is on the horizon. Indeed, CEO Elon Musk says Tesla 's will begin mass commercial production of its so-called Optimus humanoid by the end of next year.

Tesla shares aren't an investment in advanced robotics, though. It's still first and foremost an electric vehicle outfit, and robotaxis feature as prominently as robotics do in Tesla's foreseeable future. And most other up-and-coming AI robot makers are either not publicly traded or aren't worth investing in, or aren't pure plays, either.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

There may soon be one exception, however. A company called Agility Robotics -- maker of the humanoid robot called Digit -- will soon be going public. Here's what interested investors need to know.

The numbers we know so far

Robotics (including low-functioning robots) isn't exactly anything new. But Agility's Digit represents a major leap in robotic technology . The two-armed, two-legged automaton can lift up to 50 pounds, handling almost any basic task that a real person can. Although it's not going to be performing surgery or practicing law anytime soon, as of late last year, these robots had collectively moved over 100,000 totes within one of its customers' warehouses.

Granted, having been a standalone entity since 2015, Agility Robotics has had time. The current version of its Digit android is this tech's fifth generation.

Yet, the company still lost $140 million last year on only $1.8 million in sales, while the $620 million it expects to raise through its upcoming merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC) Churchill Capital Corp XI (NASDAQ: CCXI) implies a company valuation of $2.5 billion. It's a testament to the perceived value of more than a decade's worth of developmental work on a humanoid robot that's admittedly pretty amazing, even if not yet highly deployed.

Not yet highly deployed. But that day's coming sooner or later.

Agility is ready at the market's turning point

Agility's current customer list includes GXO Logistics , Toyota Motor , and German auto parts maker Schaeffler, with its humanoid robots now operating in nine different locations.

The company is going public at a time that's proving to be a major turning point for humanoid robotics in general, and for Agility Robotics' Digit in particular. Agility says it's got over $300 million worth of orders for the Digit 5 already lined up, while a recent outlook from Global Market Insights suggests the worldwide warehouse robotics market alone could grow by 23% per year through 2034, from less than $15 billion in 2024 to more than $117 billion by then.

Story Continues

The kicker: Agility Robotics' business model is designed to brilliantly capitalize on this growing demand. See, it's not just a designer and seller of advanced robotics. It's selling "robotics as a service," or RAAS. Assuming a five-year lifespan, each of these robots represents on the order of $400,000 to $500,000 worth of revenue to Agility. Moreover, that's still a net cost savings to the company's customers.

Its factory in Salem, Oregon, by the way, can currently manufacture on the order of 10,000 units per year. That's still not the scale that Musk is envisioning for Tesla's Optimus, but Agility Robotics is arguably taking more calculated aim at an industrial/goods-handling market with a more marketable work-minded solution.

What should investors do?

But is the public offering something worth at least attempting to participate in?

First (although not foremost), the upcoming offering isn't a typical initial public offering -- or IPO -- in the sense that the company will be selling newly issued shares of itself directly to its very first investors in exchange for predetermined amount of cash. There's no new offering at all, in fact. This company will be absorbed into the aforementioned Churchill Capital Corp XI, which will then become Agility Robotics.

Buying into CCXI shares today will give you a position in this company when the special acquisition actually happens, even though the official date for the completion of this transaction hasn't been announced yet. The usual speculation surrounding new and relatively unknown opportunities is still palpable, though.

While the implied $2.5 billion valuation makes no fundamental sense compared to $300 million worth of future sales (with no specific timeframe attached to that number, by the way), there's no denying there's opportunity ahead for autonomous manual-labor robots. Agility says nearly 2 million U.S. manufacturing jobs could go unfilled by 2033. It's just a question of when robots will start moving in earnest into the mainstream.

Some investors will price this stock like it's happening a week from now. Others will price this ticker as if it could take a decade. This stock is sure to waffle back and forth between these two extremes in the meantime, dishing out the same sort of volatility that shares of Space Exploration Technologies (aka SpaceX) have since the June initial public offering.

And that may be the most important takeaway here at this time. As much as investors might wish this stock would trade in a way and at a price that made some semblance of sense, that's not likely to happen anytime soon. All we know for sure is that, statistically speaking, most technology IPOs are down for the first several months following their public offering, largely thanks to the wind-down of their early but unsustainable bullish buzz. Only time will tell if that's how things will pan out for this particular SPAC.

Given the potential downside if that's in the cards, though, nobody should be in a big a hurry to dive into a big position early on and then hold on for dear life. If there are gains to be enjoyed here, Agility Robotics shares should produce them consistently once all the volatility of becoming a publicly traded outfit has run its course.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold Cisco Stock After a 68% Rise in a Year?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO shares have surged 68% over the past year, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector, which rose 27.9%.

The company's shares have also outperformed peers, including Arista Networks ANET and Broadcom AVGO. Both Arista Networks and Broadcom are expanding their footprints in the data center infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI) networking space. Shares of Arista Networks and Broadcom have rallied 52% and 3.1%, respectively, over the past year.

The outperformance can be attributed to the accelerating AI infrastructure investments, strong hyperscaler demand and a multiyear networking upgrade cycle. The growing adoption of Silicon One platforms, optical networking solutions and campus networking products, alongside strengthening demand for cybersecurity, Splunk and observability solutions, is driving growth.

CSCO Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

CSCO Benefits From AI Push & Strong Networking Growth

Cisco is benefiting from accelerating AI infrastructure investments, strong networking demand and an expanding portfolio of security and observability solutions. The growing adoption of agentic AI is driving demand for high-bandwidth, low-latency networking infrastructure across hyperscale data centers, enterprises and cloud environments, strengthening Cisco's growth prospects.

Cisco's AI infrastructure business continues to gain momentum. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the company secured $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders, bringing fiscal 2026 orders to $9.3 billion, approximately 4.5 times the previous year's level. The company's Silicon One architecture, particularly its P200 and G200-powered systems and Acacia optical solutions, is strengthening its competitive position. Cisco expects hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenues to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027 compared with approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Strong networking demand has been noteworthy. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, networking revenues surged 28% year over year, supported by triple-digit growth in AI infrastructure and double-digit growth in data center switching. Networking product orders increased 40%, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Data center networking orders grew more than 35%, while campus networking orders increased 20%, reflecting strong demand for infrastructure upgrades.

CSCO Benefits From Expanding Security Portfolio

Cisco Systems is benefiting from its expanding security portfolio, growing adoption of AI-driven cybersecurity solutions and strengthening Splunk momentum. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Security revenues increased 14% year over year to $2.23 billion. The entire security portfolio, including Splunk, recorded double-digit order growth.

More than 1,500 customers purchased Secure Access, XDR, Hypershield and AI Defense, bringing total net new customers to more than 6,400 since launch. Firewall orders increased more than 30%. The company expects security and observability growth to improve to high single digits in fiscal 2027.

Further expanding its portfolio, in August 2026, Cisco expanded its Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA NVDA through a partnership with Supermicro, strengthening its AI infrastructure portfolio with rack-scale computing solutions.

The expanded offering integrates Supermicro's liquid- and air-cooled servers with Cisco's AI networking systems, enabling enterprises, neoclouds and sovereign clouds to efficiently manage large-scale AI workloads. Supporting NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Rubin NVL8 platforms, the architecture facilitates trillion-parameter model training and high-throughput inference. Cisco's NVIDIA Cloud Partner-compliant architecture aims to simplify AI deployment, enhance security, and accelerate infrastructure scalability.

Story Continues

CSCO Initiates Positive Q1 2027 Guidance

Cisco's outlook for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 remains strong, driven by strong AI demand, accelerating networking investments and improving security momentum.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be in the range of $1.32-$1.34 per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Cisco's first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues is pegged at $18.09 billion, suggesting growth of 21.54% year over year.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $1.33 per share, up by a penny over the past 30 days and indicating 33% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

Cisco Systems, Inc. Price and Consensus

Cisco Systems, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Cisco Systems, Inc. Quote

CSCO Shares Are Trading at a Premium

Cisco's shares are trading at a premium, as suggested by the Value Score of F.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, CSCO is trading at a premium of 6.24X, higher than the Computer & Technology sector's 6.1X.

CSCO Valuation

Conclusion

Cisco's strong AI infrastructure momentum, robust networking demand and expanding security portfolio are expected to drive long-term growth. Rising hyperscaler investments, growing adoption of Silicon One and improving Splunk momentum further strengthen its growth prospects. These factors justify its premium valuation.

news.Title: Tesla Trades at 219x Earnings. Here’s Why I’m Not Buying the Bet on Its Future.
news.Content:
As of October 12, Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA ) shares have climbed about 3% over the past five days. The rally began after Q3 deliveries came in at 486,532, well above the roughly 462,000 analysts expected. Deliveries were still down about 2% from a year earlier, though. More European countries have also approved Tesla's supervised FSD software. Even after the bounce, the stock is down about 15% this year. All eyes are now on its Q3 earnings, due October 21. TSLA's next catalyst may be earnings, but its longer-term prospects are worth watching too. See why Tesla ranks third among 10 stocks that could change the world by 2030 .

Investors Are Buying the Future

On October 6, Goldman Sachs made a point I agree with. It said Tesla's stock will move more on robotaxi, FSD, and Optimus updates than on quarterly earnings. Goldman kept a Neutral rating with a $360 price target, below where the stock trades today. That says a lot about how the market values Tesla. The car business is barely growing, yet the stock trades as if robotaxis and robots are already working at scale. Tesla has started putting its Cybercab into limited service in Austin. But Waymo already completes over 500,000 paid rides a week across 15 U.S. cities, so Tesla still has a lot of ground to cover. The company has big ambitions in autonomous driving and robotics, but how does it compare with ARK Invest's other high-conviction picks ?

The Valuation Asks Investors to Wait Until 2029

Tesla's valuation is hard to defend on current earnings. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 219.06x sits about 81% above its 5-year average of 121.30x. The forward Price-to-sales ratio of 14.08x is also about 35% above its average of 10.41x. With multiples that high, you'd expect the EPS trajectory to be exceptional. But analysts expect growth of just 5% in 2026 and 23% in 2027. The big jumps only come later, with growth of 51% in 2028 and 101% in 2029. Even based on 2029 earnings, the P/E would still be about 59x. Tesla held about $34.4 billion more in cash and short-term investments than outstanding debt at the end of Q2, providing financial flexibility for its AI investments. Still, the stock leaves little room for delays, and robotaxi timelines have slipped before.

Fewer hedge funds held Tesla in Q2, with the count falling from 123 in Q1 to 116 in Q2. The value of their stakes, though, edged up from $23.1 billion to $23.8 billion.

Tesla's future could be huge if robotaxis and Optimus deliver. But based on the numbers, I don't think the stock is worth buying at this price. Investors are paying today for earnings that may not arrive until 2029, and even then the stock wouldn't look cheap.

Story Continues

While we acknowledge the potential of TSLA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Dear Apple Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 16
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) is getting ready to turn a new page in its iPhone playbook, and Oct. 16 could be a big day for the tech giant. After years of refining its familiar smartphone design, Apple is finally stepping into the foldable phone market with the iPhone Duo, a book-style device that opens up into a larger display. But with a starting price of $1,999, this is hardly an impulse purchase.

Unveiled last month, the iPhone Duo marks Apple's latest attempt to shake up its smartphone lineup and take on the growing foldable market. Now, the countdown is on. Pre-orders open on Friday, Oct. 16 at 5 a.m. Pacific Time (8 a.m. Eastern Time), ahead of the official Oct. 23 launch. Apple is also opening its "Get Ready" process on Monday, Oct. 12, allowing prospective buyers to select their preferred configuration, arrange payment and trade-in details, and prepare their orders in advance. With reports of production issues raising the possibility of limited initial supplies, getting everything ready beforehand could give buyers a head start.

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Sets the Record Straight on Terafab. What It Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks.

Why Super Micro Stock Is Heading to $60

A $1.3 Billion Reason Why IONQ Stock Is Down Today

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

The launch comes at an interesting time for Apple shareholders. While excitement around the foldable iPhone helped lift AAPL stock in September, recent reports of reduced component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro models have raised fresh demand concerns. With the iPhone Duo about to make its debut, can Apple's latest hardware gamble reignite investor enthusiasm?

About Apple Stock

Based in Cupertino, California, Apple has grown from a computer maker into one of the biggest names in global technology. Its products, including the iPhone, Mac, and iPad, have become part of everyday life for millions of people.

Beyond devices, Apple has built a thriving Services business covering the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, and Apple Pay. These offerings keep customers connected to its ecosystem while generating recurring revenue. Backed by its strong brand, loyal customer base, and broad product lineup, Apple commands a staggering market capitalization of $4.9 trillion.

AAPL stock has had a few bumps along the way in 2026, but the ride has turned out pretty well for investors who stayed patient. The year began with uncertainty around interest rates, geopolitical tensions, and the market's obsession with artificial intelligence (AI) weighing on big tech. Apple shares struggled to find their footing early on, before gradually picking up momentum as resilient iPhone demand, steady Services growth, and renewed interest in the company's AI ambitions helped shift sentiment.

Story Continues

This morning, Oct. 13, AAPL stock was hitting a new all-time high of $347.93. So far it has gained roughly 27% year-to-date (YTD) and 40% over the past 52 weeks. Part of the appeal is Apple's relatively measured approach to AI spending. Unlike some rivals pouring enormous sums into data center infrastructure, Apple has taken a more restrained route, potentially giving it room to monetize AI across its massive installed base without shouldering the same level of infrastructure costs.

This year's rise hasn't been without some bumps, though. Shares recently slipped after a report indicated that Apple had asked suppliers to cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by roughly 15% to 20% versus initial estimates. Higher prices may be cooling demand, with Apple reportedly raising the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by $100 to $1,199 and $1,299, respectively.

The broader memory and storage chip shortage, fueled by booming AI data center demand, has added to the pressure, pushing up costs across consumer electronics. Still, the demand picture is not entirely gloomy. Deepwater Asset Management's Gene Munster noted that delivery lead times for the iPhone 18 Pro had fallen 31%, while those for the Pro Max increased 1%. Combined, lead times were roughly in line with last year's iPhone 17 Pro lineup. For investors, the question now is whether Apple's latest rally can hold up if premium iPhone demand starts losing some of its shine.

Technically, Apple stock is showing mixed signals. Its 14-day RSI sits around 60, suggesting moderately positive momentum without entering overbought territory. However, the MACD line has slipped below its signal line, accompanied by a negative histogram, hinting that bullish momentum may be losing steam. Although the chart looks encouraging, a little caution would not hurt.

Apple stock is not exactly being sold at a bargain-bin price, and Wall Street knows it. Trading at roughly 38.1 times forward adjusted earnings and 10.28 times sales, AAPL commands a premium to its historical averages and several mega-cap tech peers. Investors are clearly willing to pay up for its sticky ecosystem, loyal customers, and impressive cash-generating machine.

But there's a little something extra for shareholders, too. Apple has raised its dividend for 13 consecutive years, while its roughly 12% payout ratio leaves plenty of room for future increases. With billions of dollars in stock buybacks, Apple continues to reward investors.

What You Should Know About the iPhone Duo Before Launch

Apple's first foldable iPhone brings a fresh twist to its familiar smartphone lineup. The iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch cover screen for everyday use and a 7.6-inch folding display that opens up more room for watching videos, gaming, working, and multitasking. It is also Apple's thinnest iPhone yet when unfolded, with an interface that adapts to the phone's orientation. For instance, users can watch a video on one half of the screen while keeping playback controls on the other.

Apple has also paid particular attention to the engineering behind the foldable design. Rather than simply adding a hinge to a conventional smartphone, the company has developed a reinforced structure intended to make the device feel sturdy in everyday use. Its hinge and frame incorporate support ribs and ceramic-fiber inserts at key points, with Apple claiming that the fibers are three times stronger than Grade 5 titanium. The display itself uses a thin screen layer, a custom nano-texture finish, and multilayer lamination to help reduce the visibility of the crease where the screen folds while supporting durability.

Under the hood, Apple's A20 Pro processor works alongside a new cooling system to deliver 35% higher sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. The device pairs the A20 Pro chip with 12 GB of RAM, 256 GB of base storage, and Apple's new iOS 27 operating system.

For photography, it features a dual rear-camera system with two 48-megapixel sensors. Battery life is another key consideration, particularly with two displays in the mix. Apple rates the iPhone Duo for up to 44 hours of video playback using the external screen and up to 31 hours on the larger folding display, although actual results will vary with usage and settings. Starting at $1,999, the iPhone Duo sits firmly in the premium smartphone category.

A Snapshot of Apple's Q3 Results

In July, the tech giant reported fiscal Q3 2026 results, generating revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16.4% year-over-year (YoY) and ahead of Wall Street's expectations. Adjusted earnings came in at $1.91 per share, while reported EPS climbed 28.7% to $2.02. The company also set June-quarter revenue records for the iPhone, Mac, and Services, while its installed base surpassed 2.5 billion active devices for the first time.

As usual, the iPhone did much of the heavy lifting, and its revenue jumped 22% YoY to $54.3 billion, with the iPhone 17 lineup driving record June-quarter sales across every geographic segment. Macs were another bright spot, with revenue surging 28.7% to $10.4 billion as the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro attracted both first-time buyers and customers upgrading older devices. Supply constraints did limit some sales, but demand remained encouraging.

Meanwhile, Services revenue rose 12% to a record $30.7 billion, while paid subscriptions crossed 1.5 billion. From the App Store and AppleCare to cloud services, payments, and entertainment, the business is becoming an increasingly important contributor to Apple's growth. Not every product category shared the same momentum, however. iPad revenue slipped 6% to $6.2 billion, while Wearables, Home, and Accessories revenue increased 6.5% to $7.9 billion.

Apple's financial strength adds another layer to the picture. The company ended the quarter with $147 billion in cash and marketable securities against $84 billion in debt. Record operating cash flow of $34.4 billion helped fund $33 billion in shareholder returns, including substantial stock buybacks and dividends.

Looking ahead, Apple is scheduled to report its fiscal Q4 results on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. The company expects revenue to grow 9% to 11% YoY, with iPhone sales rising in the mid-teens and Services maintaining a similar growth pace to Q3. However, currency headwinds could shave 2.5 percentage points off growth, while tighter supply and higher memory costs may pressure margins. Existing inventory, lower costs elsewhere, and a favorable product mix could help cushion the impact.

Analysts monitoring the company remain pretty confident about Apple, predicting Q4 revenue around $113.6 billion, while EPS is anticipated to rise by 7% YoY to $1.98. Looking further ahead to fiscal 2026, profit is expected to be around $8.75 per share, up 17.3% YOY, before surging another 8.8% annually to $9.52 per share in fiscal 2027.

What Do Analysts Expect for AAPL Stock?

Jim Cramer thinks Wall Street may be sleeping on Apple's biggest upcoming opportunity: the iPhone Duo. In October, the CNBC host urged investors who don't own Apple shares to consider buying on further dips before the foldable phone launches. He believes investors are underestimating how much the Duo could move the stock.

Cramer pushed back against Morgan Stanley's more cautious outlook, arguing that near-term supply concerns shouldn't overshadow the device's long-term potential. He also noted that new CEO John Ternus sounded confident about having enough units available to meet demand. For Cramer, the Duo could be a bigger deal than Wall Street expects.

AAPL stock carries a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating, reflecting a mix of optimism and caution on Wall Street. Among the 40 analysts covering the stock, 20 have issued a "Strong Buy" recommendation, while three rate it a "Moderate Buy." Meanwhile, 14 analysts have a more neutral "Hold" stance. On the bearish side, one analyst recommends a "Moderate Sell," while the remaining two are outright skeptical, advising a "Strong Sell" rating.

AAPL stock is currently trading above its average analyst price target of $331.58, but the Street-high target price of $400 suggests that the stock could rally as much as 14%.

news.Title: Demand for the iPhone 18 Is Reportedly Weak. Is Apple's Stock in Trouble?
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL)'s stock has been surging more than 30% in the past six months. It's been on a tear, as there's plenty of optimism of late surrounding the company and its new CEO, John Ternus.

However, with a heightened valuation also come high expectations. And that could potentially be problematic for Apple, as according to a recent report, it may be reducing production of its latest iPhone models due to low demand. Could the tech stock be due for a pullback before the end of 2026?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max doesn't appear to be strong

According to Nikkei Asia, demand hasn't been strong out of the gate for Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models, to the point that the company is telling its suppliers to reduce production of components related to them. Higher prices may be impacting demand, although customers may also be holding off on making a purchase until Apple's foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, comes out later this month.

There may inevitably be multiple factors that are at play here, and this doesn't guarantee that Apple's iPhone sales will be weak across all of its models. But at the same time, investors shouldn't ignore the risk that perhaps higher prices may be impacting demand this time around. Apple has had to raise prices to offset higher memory costs. And while a foldable phone may be new and exciting for Apple customers, with it starting at $1,999, it's certainly not cheap, and it'll be a big test to see how strong the demand is at such a price point.

Apple's stock may be vulnerable to a correction

Next month, Apple will report its latest quarterly earnings numbers, and investors will have much more clarity on how strong demand is for the company's latest iPhones. It may not be easy to please Wall Street, however, as the stock is trading at more than 39 times its trailing earnings, which is a significant premium for a company that hasn't always been growing at a fast pace in recent years.

If iPhone sales come in light or there are even hints that demand may not be robust, the stock could experience a significant decline, given how expensive it is right now. While investing in the tech company is normally a good move for the long term, investors shouldn't ignore its valuation, as buying Apple stock at its current inflated levels could make it difficult to generate a strong return.

news.Title: Can Nokia's Multi-PON Line Card Meet Growing AI Connectivity Demands?
news.Content:
Nokia Corporation NOK has introduced a new 50G/25G/10G/GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network) line card to help telecom operators upgrade their fiber broadband networks with greater flexibility and lower investment risk. The innovation aims to prepare network infrastructure for the growing demands of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and high-speed connectivity.

Built on Nokia's Quillion chipset, the 16-port line card supports GPON, 10G, 25G and 50G PON technologies on every port, enabling fiber access speeds of up to 50Gbps. This allows operators to upgrade network speeds as demand grows without replacing existing infrastructure. Operators can also add higher-speed technologies when needed, helping them manage investments efficiently and create new revenue opportunities.

The company's new platform offers up to four times lower upstream latency, enabling faster data transmission and improving performance for data-intensive applications. It also includes quantum-safe encryption and authentication to protect network and user data from emerging threats, while enhanced resilience helps ensure reliable connectivity for critical services.

With general availability planned for 2027, the launch strengthens Nokia's position in fiber broadband infrastructure. The solution gives telecom operators greater flexibility to expand network capacity and meet the growing connectivity needs of AI-driven applications.

How Are Competitors Performing?

Nokia faces stiff competition from Ericsson ERIC and Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO. Ericsson is improving network performance through AI-powered 5G technology to increase data speeds, coverage and efficiency. The company is working with telecom operators to improve network capacity and reliability. Ericsson is advancing next-generation wireless technology to support automated network management and new digital services.

Cisco is developing advanced networking chips to handle growing AI workloads and improve data center performance. The company is using AI-powered tools to help businesses detect network issues and automate troubleshooting. Cisco is enhancing network management and traffic visibility to help organizations monitor performance and resolve connectivity problems more efficiently.

NOK's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Nokia shares have soared 81% over the past year against the industry's decline of 0.7%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, Nokia trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 2.25, below the industry tally of 4.67.

Story Continues

Earnings estimates for 2026 have remained static at 39 cents over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have decreased 4% to 48 cents.

Nokia currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Can Intel's New GPU and Xeon Technologies Enhance its AI Capabilities?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure portfolio with new GPU technology, advanced Xeon processor systems and open software innovations to meet the growing demand for agentic AI. Its latest offerings aim to improve computing performance, power efficiency and scalability for enterprise AI workloads.

Intel introduced the latest Xeon-based rack designs to support the computing demands of agentic AI applications. Select Xeon 6+ configurations can deliver more than 46,000 cores per rack, enabling efficient data processing, workload management and task execution. Developed with ecosystem partners, these systems use open infrastructure standards to simplify deployment and help customers scale AI operations.

The company provided new details about its Intel GPU D-series, code-named Crescent Island. Built on Intel's Xe3P architecture, the accelerator offers up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory, 1.5TB/s of memory bandwidth and 1.3 petaflops of FP8 computing performance within a 350-watt power envelope. Designed for large language models and memory-intensive inference workloads, it supports models with up to 300 billion parameters on a single card and more than one trillion parameters in an eight-GPU system.

Intel is also advancing software integration across CPUs and GPUs to simplify AI application development and deployment. Its software ecosystem supports established AI frameworks, inference runtimes and emerging open models, while the AI for Enterprise Agent Toolkit provides orchestration capabilities for production AI applications.

Additionally, Intel is collaborating with industry partners to develop standardized accelerator designs that improve compatibility and simplify integration across systems. By combining Xeon processors, specialized GPUs and open software, the company is building a flexible and cost-effective foundation for deploying AI applications at scale.

How Are Competitors Performing in the AI Space?

Intel faces competition from Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Qualcomm is strengthening its AI business with data center processors and AI accelerators. The company is collaborating with Amazon to develop custom chips for AI data centers. Qualcomm is developing energy-efficient technologies to enable faster AI processing while reducing power consumption.

AMD introduced its Helios rack-scale platform to support agentic AI workloads by combining EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs. The company is working with industry partners to provide flexible, scalable AI infrastructure for data centers. AMD is expanding its Instinct GPU portfolio to handle demanding AI training and inference workloads while improving computing performance and energy efficiency.

Story Continues

Shares of Intel have skyrocketed 184.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 32.2%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Going by the price/book ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 4.96 times book value, lower than the industry average of 23.36.

INTC's earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 2% to $1.50 per share, while those for 2027 have increased 2.1% to $1.97 over the past 60 days.
