news.Title: Intel vs. Sanmina: Which AI Infrastructure Stock is a Better Buy Now?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC and Sanmina Corporation SANM are two premier U.S.-based semiconductor firms focusing on AI (artificial intelligence), advanced chip technologies and the data center semiconductor ecosystem. While Intel focuses on semiconductor design and manufacturing, Sanmina specializes in electronics manufacturing and complex infrastructure systems.

Intel is currently focusing on AI chips for data centers and PCs, which marks one of the largest architectural shifts for the company in 40 years. The decision is primarily aimed at gaining a firmer footing in the expansive AI sector, spanning cloud and enterprise servers to networks, volume clients and ubiquitous edge environments, in tune with the evolving market dynamics. The foundry operating model is a key component of the company's strategy and is designed to reshape operational dynamics and drive greater transparency, accountability and focus on costs and efficiency.

Sanmina is a key player in the electronics manufacturing services (EMS) industry. It focuses on engineering and fabricating complex components and on providing complete end-to-end supply chain solutions to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across various end markets.

Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

The Case for INTC

Intel is witnessing healthy traction in AI PCs that have taken the market by storm. Its innovative AI solutions are set to benefit the broader semiconductor ecosystem by lowering costs, improving performance and fostering an open, scalable AI environment. The proliferation of generative AI applications is driving significant investments in data center infrastructure. Although GPUs remain at the center of AI computing, CPUs continue to play an important role in supporting AI workloads. This is creating incremental opportunities for Intel's Xeon portfolio. The momentum is encouraging as AI-related infrastructure spending is likely to remain healthy, providing Intel with an opportunity to capitalize on rising compute requirements.

Intel is ramping Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake products based on its advanced 18A process technology. Increasing adoption of these products, coupled with an eventual enterprise PC refresh cycle, should support the client business over the long run. The company is also expanding its presence in edge computing and physical AI applications, including robotics. These emerging markets could broaden Intel's addressable opportunity beyond traditional PCs.

However, Intel derives a significant part of its revenues from China. As Washington tightens restrictions on high-tech exports to China, Beijing has intensified its push for self-sufficiency in critical industries. This shift poses a dual challenge for Intel, as it faces potential market restrictions and increased competition from domestic chipmakers. The company is also lagging in the GPU and AI front compared to peers, such as NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. Leading technology companies are reportedly piling up NVIDIA's GPUs to build computing clusters for their AI work, driving exponential revenue growth.

Story Continues

The Case for SANM

Sanmina is increasingly focusing on 42Q connected manufacturing that effectively integrates data from customers' global factories and suppliers' fleets and creates an up-to-date information base. It offers a unified data ecosystem with real-time data analytics capabilities that significantly improve visibility across the enterprise's distributed manufacturing and accelerate the decision-making process. Sanmina has deployed the 42Q connected manufacturing in more than 70 factories across 15 countries, connecting more than 35,000 pieces of manufacturing equipment in the cloud. Such a technology-driven, customer-focused approach enables Sanmina to work closely with its customers to anticipate future manufacturing requirements and modify its R&D initiatives accordingly. Attracting and developing strong customer relationships by delivering high-level customer service is one of the key strategies to drive commercial expansion.

Sanmina has acquired the data center infrastructure manufacturing business from AMD to scale up production for cloud and AI hyperscale customers. It is positioning itself as an end-to-end manufacturing partner for AI data centers, spanning accelerated compute, AI racks, liquid cooling, networking, storage and power infrastructure. The company offers end-to-end solutions that include product design, manufacturing, assembly, testing and aftermarket support. Such an end-to-end approach allows clients to rely on a single partner throughout the product lifecycle management. Its vertically integrated manufacturing process brings several other advantages. This approach streamlines processes and lowers costs, enabling Sanmina to achieve greater economies of scale.

However, Sanmina has been heavily affected by supply-chain disruptions over the past few years. Owing to current geopolitical events, the company is currently experiencing delays and shortages of critical components, including capacitors, resistors and more. Management expects supply chain issues to persist in the short to medium term. Intensifying competition in the EMS industry has hurt Sanmina's net sales. The company faces stiff competition from bigger players like Jabil, Inc. JBL. It generates about 80% of its net sales from products manufactured outside the United States, which exposes it to political and economic disruptions in the operating countries. The company also has major production facilities in China. The recent imposition of tariffs on these countries by the U.S. government has increased the cost of sales and strained margins.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for INTC & SANM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Intel's 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 17.8%, while that for EPS indicates a surge of 257.1%. The EPS estimates have trended up 2% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Sanmina's fiscal 2026 sales indicates a year-over-year growth of 74.2%, while that for EPS suggests a rise of 100.5%. The EPS estimates have remained static over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of INTC & SANM

Over the past year, Intel has surged 184.4% compared with the industry's growth of 34.1%. Sanmina has gained 70.3% over the same period.

Sanmina looks more attractive than Intel from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, Intel's shares currently trade at 7.41 forward sales, higher than 0.7 for Sanmina.

INTC or SANM: Which is a Better Pick?

Both Intel and Sanmina currently carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

In terms of price performance, Intel has outperformed Sanmina, although it is trading at a slight premium. Although there is not much to choose from, INTC appears to be relatively better placed than SANM and might be a better investment option at the moment.

news.Title: Michael Burry's latest bet raises uncomfortable questions for Tesla
news.Content: Buying a new car can be a big hassle. I remember buying my first car, a Honda Accord, back in 2020, and the decision involved all the nitpicky things, like choosing a color, comparing features, and figuring out whether the monthly payment fit my budget. These days, though, that last question can end the conversation before it begins. The average new vehicle costs more than $50,000, according to Kelley Blue Book. And while electric cars promise lower running costs, their sticker prices still make shoppers hesitate. That's why, amidst a sea of Michael Burry headlines, his latest investment caught my attention. The 'Big Short' investor famous for anticipating the 2008 housing crash has scooped up shares in a Tesla ( TSLA ) rival whose appeal, in his view, is that it's able to build cars for less. Tesla, meanwhile, is asking investors to believe in much more than the cars it sells. Its enormous stock-market valuation reflects hopes for autonomous driving, robotics, and businesses that remain works in progress. Both ideas could prove right. A manufacturer can be efficient without winning every customer, and Tesla may eventually deliver on its ambitions. But as Americans weigh what they can afford, Burry's move begs the question: Is Tesla's future worth the premium investors are paying today? Michael Burry buys Tesla rival as a massive valuation gap draws attention Michael Burry added shares of Chinese automaker BYD in an October 6 portfolio reshuffle, according to a Substack update cited by Seeking Alpha on October 12 . More Wall Street: Nvidia and Micron are about to lord their successes all over Wall Street Nvidia, Palantir, and Alphabet send waves through Wall Street Wall Street elites will pocket windfall from record $46 billion profits That said, how many shares he bought and how much he paid remain undisclosed. "BYD is potentially the lowest-cost producer of vehicles in the world thanks to its vertically integrated model at scale," he wrote in earlier analysis. He pointed to the company's in-house batteries, manufacturing expertise, and overseas expansion. Now consider the valuation gap. At the October 9 close, Tesla was worth around $1.51 trillion, according to Stock Analysis , while BYD stood near $104 billion. Yet BYD reported about $111 billion in revenue for 2025, according to the 311 Institute , compared with Tesla's $94.8 billion, according to the companies' annual disclosures. That's a massive 14.5-to-one gap in market value. That doesn't mean Tesla is necessarily overpriced, though. BYD sells plug-in hybrids as well as battery-powered vehicles, while Tesla's valuation reflects its 'other bets', which include robotaxis, energy storage, and robotics beyond car sales. Story Continues Given the impact of its other businesses, many of which are speculative, Tesla stock is trading at over 218 times non-GAAP forward earnings according to Seeking Alpha . Burry's skepticism of Elon Musk's automaker isn't new, though. His firm held bearish Tesla options in 2021, and Musk later dismissed him as a "broken clock." In June 2026, Burry disclosed another Tesla short at $416.22 a share, but there's no confirmation he still holds it as reported by Electrek . However, for me, what's most revealing is what Burry chose to buy, which is a manufacturer he believes can build cars at a lower cost. Tesla faces an affordability challenge as Americans rethink car purchases Americans paid an average of $50,089 for a new vehicle in August, according to Kelley Blue Book . Moreover, financing one is far from being painless. Experian says the average new-car loan payment reached $765 a month in the second quarter . That's roughly 39% higher compared to Q2 2019, when the payment was around $550. Tesla isn't immune to that squeeze. Its average U.S. transaction price was $52,616 in August, above the overall market but below the $54,813 average for electric vehicles, Kelley Blue Book found . So even though Tesla might not be unusually pricey compared with its EV competitors, electric cars remain a costly purchase for many households. The tension shows up in online discussions. After test-driving a 2026 Model Y, one Reddit user loved the experience but admitted, "As much as I'd love the 2026 one, I drove with how quiet it was on the road, and the interior, new design, and the awesome-looking steering wheel, I'm not sure I can afford it." That's exactly what has piqued Burry's interest in BYD. The Chinese manufacturer produces its own Blade batteries and integrates major powertrain components, giving it greater control over production costs. Its lineup also includes smaller vehicles Tesla doesn't sell, including the Dolphin Surf, listed in France from €19,990 for the base model. There's a catch for American shoppers: BYD passenger cars aren't broadly available in the United States, where tariffs and trade barriers limit Chinese vehicle competition. BYD Executive Vice President Stella Li recently acknowledged that the company has been considering entering the U.S. market for a "long time." "We don't have clarity, visibility and stability there," she added, "so we're saying let's hold and not to go to the US for passenger cars at this moment." Still, Burry's bet raises a bigger question: Which automakers can deliver vehicles households can actually afford? Tesla's next earnings report could test Wall Street's lofty expectations Tesla's pricing setup rests on more than the vehicles leaving its factories. Investors are betting that robotaxis, self-driving software, humanoid robots, and energy storage will become major profit engines, but as I remarked earlier, a lot of these businesses remain too speculative to materially change the operational framework. For now, the car business still matters. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3, beating analysts' expectations despite a 2.1% decline from a year earlier, as reported by Electrek . Its Supercharger network, software, and customer loyalty give it advantages a lower sticker price cannot erase. Interestingly, Burry's preferred automaker faces problems. BYD's 2025 net profit fell 19%, according to Reuters , as competition squeezed margins. Demand in China remains relatively weak, while trade restrictions complicate overseas expansion. That makes Tesla's October 21 earnings report especially important. I'll be watching Tesla's automotive profit margins and free cash flow, as well as capital spending and evidence of progress in autonomy, robotics, and energy. Those figures should help show whether Tesla's existing automotive business can support the future investors are paying for. Burry's purchase doesn't prove Tesla is overvalued. It exposes the tension: Americans need cars they can afford, while Tesla shareholders are paying for ambitions that extend well beyond selling them. The company delivered 478,237 Model 3/Y vehicles and 8,295 other models compared with 481,166 and 15,933 units, respectively, in the year-ago quarter. The decline was primarily concentrated in other models, whose deliveries fell 47.9%.

A key factor behind the year-over-year decline is the challenging comparison with the third quarter of 2025, when Tesla delivered a record 497,099 vehicles amid a rush to purchase electric vehicles (EVs) before the expiration of the $7,500 U.S. federal EV tax credit on Sept. 30, 2025. This demand pull-forward boosted the year-ago quarter's deliveries. Despite the year-over-year decrease, Tesla's third-quarter 2026 deliveries rose 1.3% sequentially, supported by a recovery in European sales and stronger demand for China-made vehicles in international markets. China-made Model 3 and Model Y sales, including exports, increased 5% year over year in September.

We expect revenues from automotive sales to be $20.69 billion, while automotive gross margin is projected at 17.3%. Vehicle deliveries, pricing and production costs are likely to have influenced the company's automotive performance in the to-be-reported quarter.

Tesla's Energy Generation and Storage segment remains a potential growth driver, supported by demand for its Megapack and Powerwall products. The company deployed 13.7 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage products in the third quarter, up 9.6% from the year-ago period and 1.5% from 13.5 GWh in the second quarter of 2026. news.Title: NVIDIA Begins Vera Rubin Production: Can It Extend NVDA's AI Lead?
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation 's NVDA Vera Rubin platform could extend its lead in the artificial intelligence (AI) market by delivering greater computing performance and efficiency for increasingly complex AI workloads. Production of this next-generation platform has started, giving NVIDIA another opportunity to strengthen its position as businesses expand AI infrastructure.

The platform combines Rubin GPUs (graphics processing units), Vera CPUs (Central Processing Units), networking, storage and other components into integrated systems designed for large-scale AI factories. NVIDIA claims Vera Rubin can deliver 10 times the agent throughput of its previous Grace Blackwell platform at scale. Its production network spans more than 350 factories across 30 countries.

The growth opportunity is substantial. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA's revenues increased 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, while Data Center revenues climbed 117% to $89 billion. Management expects third-quarter revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and anticipates Vera Rubin will contribute about 20% of Data Center revenues in the quarter.

Major cloud providers, including CoreWeave, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle and Nebius, are preparing to deploy the platform. These partnerships could help NVIDIA capture demand for AI agents that perform multi-step tasks, increasing the need for computing power.

Vera Rubin strengthens NVIDIA's growth outlook. However, supply constraints could limit its ability to meet demand, while rising memory costs could pressure margins. Management expects supply to remain a bottleneck through at least fiscal 2028.

NVIDIA's Rivals Advance Their AI Chip Platforms

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD is challenging NVIDIA with its Instinct GPUs and Helios rack-scale systems. AMD's second-quarter 2026 revenues rose 50% year over year to $11.54 billion, while Data Center sales jumped 107% to $6.72 billion.

Advanced Micro Devices also plans to supply up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 GPUs to Anthropic, with the first deployment expected in the first half of 2027. This could make AMD a stronger alternative as customers seek more AI computing capacity.

Intel Corporation INTC is also expanding its data-center business. Its second-quarter 2026 revenues rose 25% year over year to $16.13 billion, supported by demand for its processor products.

Intel is investing in its CPU, advanced packaging and manufacturing capabilities to capture more AI infrastructure spending. However, NVIDIA's integrated GPU systems, networking and software ecosystem remain important advantages.

Story Continues

Advanced Micro Devices' upcoming MI450 platform and Intel's processor business offer customers more choices. Still, NVIDIA's Vera Rubin ramp could help it maintain its lead if it delivers the promised performance and scales production smoothly.

news.Title: Is Tesla (TSLA) a Car Market Leader or a $1 Trillion Robotics Gamble?
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) opened October with a sales number worth celebrating. The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, following a second quarter that was already its best Q2 on record. Here's the twist. Car sales aren't what holds up the share price.

Tesla still makes most of its money selling electric vehicles, overwhelmingly the Model 3 and Model Y. It also sells Megapack and Powerwall batteries to utilities and homeowners, and earns a fast-growing slice from services, including subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software. But the Tesla investors are paying for a different company: one that runs robotaxis, builds humanoid robots, and turns software into profit, shaping the kind of transformative vision highlighted among 10 Stocks That Will Change the World by 2030 . So the real question isn't whether the car business is recovering. It's whether that recovery buys Tesla enough time to prove everything else.

The Moat Is Moving Into Software

Tesla's old edge was manufacturing EVs at scale before anyone else could. That advantage matters less as more automakers sell electric cars, which is why the stronger evidence now sits in software.

Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.48 million in Q2, up 56% from a year earlier and up from 1.28 million in Q1. In North America, more than 55% of new deliveries came with an FSD subscription attached. That's recurring revenue (income that repeats monthly, not once at the sale), riding on a fleet that keeps feeding driving data back to Tesla. Owning the fleet, the chips, and the software stack together puts it among the stocks shaping autonomous driving .

Services and other revenue grew 50% in Q2, the fastest of Tesla's three reporting lines.

From Slides to Factory Floors

Q2 showed the moonshots turning into hardware. Cybercab production has begun at Gigafactory Texas, where Tesla lists installed capacity above 125,000 units a year. Robotaxi service runs in seven metro areas, with Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, and Tampa ramping unsupervised, and the San Francisco Bay Area operating with a safety driver. In Fremont, the old Model S and X lines were pulled out to make room for the first Optimus robot lines.

Energy is pulling its weight too. Storage deployments hit 13.5 GWh in Q2, up 41% year over year, then rose to 13.7 GWh in Q3, a surging momentum that highlights why momentum is building across the 10 Best Battery Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires . None of this is cheap. Tesla describes this as its largest investment period, and capital spending reached $5.8 billion in Q2, up 142% from a year earlier.

Story Continues

Can the Cars Keep Paying for the Robots?

That spending is exactly what worries investors, and CNBC's coverage of Q2 centered on sliding margins and free cash flow turning negative. The numbers back it up. Revenue climbed 26% to $28,236 million, yet income from operations fell 57% to $398 million, leaving a GAAP operating margin of just 1.4%. Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) came in at negative $1,092 million.

GAAP net income of $1,114 million was well above that $398 million operating profit, so the core business earned less than the bottom line suggests. Still, Tesla isn't running on fumes. Operating cash flow jumped 85% to $4,697 million, and the company holds $43,524 million in cash and investments. The risk isn't a cash crunch. It's years of thin profits if the new businesses ramp slower than hoped.

A Price Tag Written in the Future Tense

At 218.80 times forward earnings, as of October 9, Tesla trades far above its own 5-year average of 121.43 and the sector's 14.78. In plain terms, investors are paying almost $219 for every $1 of expected earnings, while a typical sector peer costs under $15.

Expected EPS growth of 24.78% in 2027 is healthy. But that pace alone doesn't explain a triple-digit multiple, let alone one well above Tesla's own history. The gap is the autonomy and robotics premium, the kind usually reserved for early-stage AI platform stories, raising questions similar to whether Can Palantir (PLTR) Justify a Multiple that's 5 Times the Sector's? With Q2 non-GAAP EPS down 18% to $0.33, earnings are currently moving the wrong way for the multiple to shrink on its own.

Big money has cooled a little. Hedge fund interest declined, with 116 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, down from 123 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 1.95% of the float, which points to relatively limited bearish positioning.

Where the Evidence Points

The car rebound is real, energy is growing, and FSD subscriptions are compounding. But at 218.80 times forward earnings, the stock already assumes robotaxis and Optimus become major profit engines. That setup suits long-horizon investors who believe in autonomy and can stomach several quarters of heavy spending. If you want valuation support today, there isn't much of it. Q3 results later this month are the next test: a margin recovery alongside high spending would strengthen the case, while another quarter of negative free cash flow would make the premium harder to defend.

While we acknowledge the potential of TSLA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Applied Materials (AMAT) Trades at 39.66 Times Earnings. Can 2027 Growth Carry It?
news.Content: Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT ) keeps adding heavyweight partners. Intel recently agreed to work with the company on next-generation transistors, interconnects, and chip packaging, just days after packaging specialist Besi expanded its own long-running collaboration. Yet the stock has spent recent weeks absorbing a very different message: worry that AI spending can't climb forever. The business is easy to describe and hard to copy. Applied sells the machines chipmakers use to deposit, etch, and shape ultra-thin layers of material on silicon wafers. It then earns steady service revenue keeping those tools running. If you've used an AI chatbot today, the chips answering you almost certainly passed through Applied's equipment. So the real question isn't whether demand is strong, even as investors look toward the other 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy Now According to Billionaires for capital allocation ideas. It's whether investors are paying a fair price for a structural boom, or a peak price for a familiar cycle. Breadth That Pays Applied's edge is reach. Advanced AI chips need many layers of materials engineering, and Applied supplies tools across a wide span of them, from transistor formation to the advanced packaging that stacks chips together. That makes it a default call when a customer adds capacity, a position that rival process-equipment makers chase in narrower slices. Pricing power shows up in the margins. Fiscal Q3 2026 marked Applied's 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion, with non-GAAP gross margin reaching 50.4%. The services arm, Applied Global Services, lifted revenue to $1,781 million from $1,463 million a year earlier, a recurring stream that cushions the lumpier equipment business. A Record Quarter, a Bigger Forecast Fiscal Q3 2026 delivered record revenue of $9.12 billion, up 25% year over year, and record non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.50, up 41%. GAAP EPS came in at $3.17, dragged down partly by swings in the value of Applied's strategic investments. The mix tells the more interesting story. DRAM, the memory that feeds AI accelerators, rose to 26% of equipment revenue from 22% a year earlier. China's share of total revenue slipped to 28% from 35%, as sales to the US, Korea, and Europe climbed. Management guided fiscal Q4 revenue to $10.25 billion, plus or minus $500 million, with non-GAAP EPS of $4.02. CEO Gary Dickerson said improved demand visibility from customers points to another strong growth year in 2027. The company is also building out a $500 million Singapore campus that more than doubles its cleanroom capacity there. Its EPIC Center partnerships, now including Broadcom, Besi, and Intel, put Applied inside customers' R&D years before tools ship, which places it alongside 11 AI Stocks That Will Go to the Moon . Story Continues This is the worry that has actually moved the stock. Last month, the heads of three leading AI labs called for slowing how fast AI models improve, and chip stocks took the hit, according to CNBC. Equipment makers feel that kind of news first, because they sell against factories that don't exist yet. That's a fair concern. Chip equipment has always been cyclical, and orders can vanish long before chip sales slow, a risk that hangs over every supplier to AI hardware . Still, nothing in Applied's reported results or guidance shows a slowdown so far. Its own forecast calls for a record quarter. The risk is real, but the evidence of it hasn't arrived. Priced Like a Grower Now At a forward P/E of 39.66, as of October 9, investors are paying $39.66 for every $1 of expected earnings. That sits well above the sector's 23.35 and far above Applied's own five-year average of 21.85. Growth is the counterweight. Analysts expect EPS to grow 44.50% in 2027, and that expected growth rate runs ahead of the forward multiple. If Applied delivers anything close to it, today's premium shrinks quickly as earnings catch up. Cash backs that up. Applied generated record operating cash flow of $3.04 billion in fiscal Q3 2026 and returned $860 million to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. Even so, the multiple leaves little margin for error. A stock priced for growth gets punished harder when growth wobbles, and that 21.85 average shows how far the multiple could fall back. Hedge fund interest dipped slightly, with 137 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, down from 138 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 1.78% of the float, a sign of relatively limited bearish positioning. Growth Has to Show Up The evidence suggests Applied's premium is buying real momentum, not just enthusiasm: expanding margins, less reliance on China, and a forecast pointing higher still. At nearly 40 times expected earnings, though, the 2027 growth story has to materialize. The setup suits growth-focused investors comfortable with semiconductor swings and a multi-year horizon. A guidance cut in the fiscal Q4 report, or clear signs that big AI customers are pausing capacity plans, would change the picture fast. news.Title: Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
news.Content:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Shares of this seller of routers, switches, software and services have returned +4.8% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +2.1% change. The Zacks Computer - Networking industry, to which Cisco belongs, has gained 2.8% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Cisco is expected to post earnings of $1.33 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +33%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.8%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $5.11 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +18%. This estimate has changed +0.1% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.59 indicates a change of +9.4% from what Cisco is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.2%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Cisco.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Cisco, the consensus sales estimate of $18.09 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +21.5%. The $73.03 billion and $77.87 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +15.3% and +6.6%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Cisco reported revenues of $17.25 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +17.6%. EPS of $1.22 for the same period compares with $0.99 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $16.85 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +2.36%. The EPS surprise was +4.27%.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Cisco is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Cisco. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Advanced Micro Devices: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence boom has transformed the technology landscape, leaving investors to choose between the companies that design powerful chips and the ones that provide the machinery to build them. Should you buy Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) or Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD)?

Applied Materials is a titan in the equipment space, selling the tools required to fabricate complex semiconductors. Advanced Micro Devices focuses on the architecture itself, designing high-performance processors for servers and PCs. Both companies sit at the heart of the digital economy, but they offer different paths to growth for investors.

The case for Applied Materials

Applied Materials provides the specialized machinery, software, and services used to manufacture chips and displays. Its global reach includes a massive footprint in China, Taiwan, and Korea, where it serves the world's largest chipmakers. In October 2026, the company expanded its partnership with Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) to focus on hardware for the semiconductor stocks market. However, its customer base is highly concentrated, with two major clients accounting for roughly 19% and 15% of revenue in fiscal 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $28.4 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.4% compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of close to $7.0 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of roughly 24.7%, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining as profit after all expenses are paid.

As of its October 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.3x. This metric compares total debt to the value of shareholder equity, with lower numbers suggesting a conservative financial structure. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term debts with assets that can be converted to cash quickly, was approximately 2.6x. Free cash flow for the year reached nearly $5.7 billion, representing the cash a business generates after accounting for the costs required to maintain or expand its physical assets.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

Advanced Micro Devices designs high-performance computing and graphics products for data centers, gaming, and PCs. In October 2025, the company secured a multiyear strategic partnership with OpenAI to deploy Instinct GPUs at significant scale. It also maintains ongoing collaborations with Sony and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) for semi-custom chips used in game consoles. The company relies on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its revenue, including hyperscale data centers and original equipment manufacturers.

Story Continues

In FY 2025, revenue surged to approximately $34.6 billion, a significant increase of roughly 34.3% over the previous year. Net income for the period reached close to $4.3 billion. The company achieved a net margin of nearly 12.5%, indicating how much profit it generates from its total sales.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1x. The current ratio is nearly 2.9x, suggesting the company maintains a robust cushion to meet its immediate financial obligations. Free cash flow for the fiscal year reached close to $6.7 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Applied Materials faces exposure to evolving export controls, particularly regarding semiconductor technology sales to China, which require complex and costly license acquisitions. High customer concentration increases volatility if major clients reduce spending or face liquidity issues. The semiconductor industry is also highly cyclical and remains sensitive to broader economic shifts. Furthermore, the company faces a $252 million settlement for export violations involving Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp .

Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition from established players like Intel and Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). It relies heavily on third-party manufacturers, primarily Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM), for wafer fabrication. Export restrictions on advanced semiconductor products to China have necessitated significant inventory charges and threaten to limit future market access. Security vulnerabilities in its hardware products could also result in reputational damage or costly remediation efforts.

Valuation comparison

Applied Materials trades at a lower multiple of future earnings estimates than its rival, potentially appealing to those looking for a more established valuation. The Forward P/E ratio compares the current stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the market value of the company relative to its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

I'd go with AMD, and honestly it is not a close call right now. In Q2 2026, AMD's data center revenue more than doubled year over year, its partnership with Anthropic signals demand that stretches well beyond the current quarter, and the company has posted six consecutive quarters of above-30% growth. AMD is cementing its position as the primary alternative to Nvidia in the AI chip market, and that is a powerful place to be.

Applied Materials is a well-run business that keeps benefiting as chip complexity grows. In its most recent quarter, AI-driven demand for advanced semiconductor equipment kept orders healthy and the outlook was positive. For investors who want diversified exposure to the chip manufacturing build-out without betting on any single end market, it is a solid choice.

But there is a difference between benefiting from a trend and being at the center of it. AMD is competing directly for the biggest prize in semiconductors right now, and the results keep arriving ahead of expectations.

news.Title: Bear Call Spread Ideas for Tesla Earnings Next Week
news.Content:
A bear call spread is a type of vertical spread, meaning that two options within the same expiry month are being traded.

One call option is being sold, which generates a credit for the trader. Another call option is bought to provide protection against an adverse move.

More News from Barchart

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

The sold call is always closer to the stock price than the bought call.

As the name suggests, this trade does best when the stock declines after the trade is opened.

However, there can be many cases where this trade can make a profit if the stock stays flat and even if it rises slightly.

Bear call spreads are risk defined trades, there are no naked options here, so they can be traded in retirement accounts such as an IRA.

Traders should have a bearish outlook on the stock and ideally look to enter when the stock has a high implied volatility rank.

Tesla (TSLA) is showing an IV Percentile of 87% in advance of their earnings announcement on June 23rd.

Assuming we have a bearish outlook on TSLA stock, we can run the Barchart's Bear Call Spread Screener and find the following results:

Below are the full parameters for this scan:

TSLA Bear Call Spread Example

Let's analyze the first line item, which has a Max Profit% of 9.94%.

This Bear Call Spread on TSLA stock involves selling the $430-strike November 13 call and buying the $455-strike call.

That spread could be sold for around $2.26 which means the trader would receive $226 into their account. The maximum risk is $2274 for a total profit potential of 9.94% with a loss probability of 14.0%.

The breakeven price is $432.26, which is 14.35% above the current stock price. This can be calculated by taking the short call strike and adding the premium received.

As the spread is $25 wide, the maximum risk in the trade is 25 – 2.26 x 100 = $2,274.

A More Aggressive Version

Let's analyze another result from the screener, this time the one with a higher Max Profit Percentage.

The example involves selling the $405-strike November 13 call and buying the $420-strike call.

That spread could be sold for around $3.30 which means the trader would receive $330 into their account. The maximum risk is $1,170, for a total profit potential of 28.21% with a loss probability of 26.8%.

Story Continues

The breakeven price is $408.30, which is 8.01% above the current stock price.

The expected move for TSLA for the November 13 expiration is between 345.99 and 410.08

Mitigating Risk

Thankfully, Bear Call Spreads are risk defined trades, so they have some built in risk management.

The most the first example can lose is $2,274 and the second example could lose a maximum of $1,170.

Position sizing is important so that a 100% loss does not cause more than a 1-2% loss in total portfolio value.

Bear Call Spreads can also contain early assignment risk, so be mindful of that if the stock breaks through the short strike and it's getting close to expiry.

Trades held over earnings can be risky as they leave little room for adjustments if the stock makes a large, adverse move.

Please remember that options are risky, and investors can lose 100% of their investment.

This article is for education purposes only and not a trade recommendation. Remember to always do your own due diligence and consult your financial advisor before making any investment decisions.

news.Title: Dear TSMC Stock Fans, Circle Oct. 15 on Your Calendar
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM), or TSMC, is slated to report its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 15. The chipmaking giant, which controls roughly 73% of the global pure-play foundry market, is benefiting greatly from the AI boom.

Yet Q3 earnings will put its growth, margins, and spending plans under the spotlight, with investors looking for signs that demand for its advanced chips is still running strong.

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Sets the Record Straight on Terafab. What It Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks.

Why Super Micro Stock Is Heading to $60

A $1.3 Billion Reason Why IONQ Stock Is Down Today

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

AI Demand Remains the Central Growth Driver

TSMC supplies semiconductor manufacturing services to major technology companies, including Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Qualcomm (QCOM), MediaTek, and Marvell Technology (MRVL). The list doesn't end here. As of 2025, TSMC manufactured 12,682 products for 534 customers. As long as the business of its customers keeps expanding and is led by the AI boom, TSMC will keep growing too.

Furthermore, manufacturing the most advanced chips requires extraordinary precision, years of process development, and the ability to manufacture chips reliably at scale. TSMC has spent billions of dollars and has years of expertise in building and upgrading semiconductor factories. Competitors cannot quickly replicate TSMC's technology, manufacturing experience, or production capacity. This is why TSMC remains in a commanding position, with Samsung Foundry second at just 7% of the global foundry market.

The company has already set a high bar with a robust second quarter, as AI-related demand remained exceptionally strong, supported by cloud service providers and the growing need for computing power. Revenue increased by 37% year over year to $40.2 billion, while earnings per share rose by 77.4%. High-performance computing (HPC) contributed 66% to total revenue. Gross margin reached 67.7%, while operating margin came in at 60.3%, driven primarily by cost-reduction efforts and better capacity utilization.

For the third quarter, management expects revenue in the range of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion. However, gross margin could be around 65% to 67%, as management expects the ramp-up of the 2-nanometer manufacturing technology to affect gross margin. Furthermore, overseas factory expansion may support future growth, but this is another factor weighing on profitability now.

Story Continues

During the Q2 earnings call, when asked about the future, CEO C.C. Wei mentioned the burgeoning agentic AI industry, in which AI systems can complete jobs through more independent, multistep processes. He believes that agentic AI can open up new options outside specialized AI accelerators. TSMC collaborates with clients utilizing several processing architectures, which may cause demand to spread over multiple categories of advanced silicon rather than relying on a single chip design.

A Bigger Investment Budget Signals Confidence but Raises the Stakes

Another important thing investors should watch out for in the third-quarter earnings is TSMC's investment plans. During the second-quarter call, management raised the full-year 2026 capital expenditure budget to between $60 billion and $64 billion, citing demand from customers and opportunities associated with AI and other computing trends. The company expects to direct 70% to 80% of its capital spending toward advanced manufacturing processes, while specialty technologies will receive about 10%. The remaining 10% to 20% will support advanced packaging, testing, mask production, and related operations.

This spending plan reflects a long-term bet on demand, but it could also put pressure on near-term cash flows and margins. New facilities and manufacturing processes require substantial investment before they can contribute meaningfully to revenue. Investors should therefore pay attention to management's comments about capacity expansion, customer commitments, and the expected pace of future investment.

What Does Wall Street Say About TSM Stock?

On Wall Street, TSMC holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Out of 19 analysts with coverage, 16 rate TSM stock as a "Strong Buy," two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and one analyst offers a "Hold" rating. TSM stock has surged 41.8% year-to-date (YTD), outpacing the overall market's gain. The average price target of $518.36 suggests the stock can gain 14.3% from current levels. The high target price of $665 implies potential upside of 47% over the next 12 months.

news.Title: 亞股低氣壓! 台股盤中大跌1235點 失守4萬9
news.Content:
[ 非凡新聞 ]記者謝旻蓁,攝影林家弘

台股今（13）日賣壓沉重，指數盤中大跌超過1200點，跌破4萬9千點大關，電子族群普遍走弱，DRAM、矽光子更是淪為重災區，拖累大盤終場下跌960點，收在48341點，成交量約1.19兆元。儘管證交所出面喊話，資本市場有一定支撐，會密切關注政經情勢變化，不過投資人信心還是沒有回籠，從籌碼面來看，三大法人周二合計賣超台股1984億元，其中，外資大砍1653億，創史上第三大賣超紀錄，也讓新台幣兌美元在盤中跟著貶值超過3角，雖然央行尾盤調節之下收32.085元，但仍重貶1.9角，還爆出史上第二大成交量，合計台北與元太外匯經紀公司達54.33億美元。

台股盤面一片綠油油，因為美股重挫、日韓股13日也開低，拖累台股跟著大跳水，指數盤中重挫超過1200點，跌破4萬9千點整數大關，而且不只大型權值股遭到拋售，中小型股也難敵賣壓，櫃買指數同樣走跌。

群益期貨分析師 徐楨榕：「費半在獲利最好跟成長性最好的板塊遭受獲利了結，多少會影響到台股的情緒，記憶體板塊，特別是韓股的部分今天是重挫，當然會連帶影響到近日的台股，多少是用融資攻起來的，通常整數的關卡其實都會稍微回測到將近3%的附近，可能大概會落在4萬8到4萬8500。」

觀察盤面類股表現，台積電力守2500元，台達電跌約半根停板，DRAM概念股雖然財報表現亮眼卻利多不漲，南亞科、華邦電紛紛重挫，光通訊聯亞、光聖也同步回檔，只剩金融、塑化等非電族群逆勢抗跌。

就怕台股急挫引發投資人恐慌，證交所也趕緊出面喊話，表示台股因為跟國際市場連動高，現在受到多重因素影響短期波動，股價出現變化，不過台股資本市場還是有一定支撐，證交所將會密切關注相關情形。專家也表示，在短線反應過後，接下來仍持續看好企業獲利動能。

華南投顧董事長 呂仁傑：「往明年看我們認為在台股這邊來看，台股企業獲利的狀況今年往明年看，應該還有2到3成左右的增長幅度，市場應該在經歷10月這邊的修正之後，往11月來看整個行情應該還是向上的，我們看今年第四季就有機會挑戰5萬3千點。」

除了內資有信心外資同樣很樂觀，高盛最新報告再喊加碼，還給出法人圈最高目標價，預估台股未來12個月有望衝上57500點，所以在國際利空變數淡化，大盤還是有機會重返基本面主導格局。（記者謝旻蓁、林家弘／台北採訪報導）

news.Title: Not Tesla. Not Nvidia. Elon Musk's Chip Ambitions Could Supercharge This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock.
news.Content:
Elon Musk has his eyes set on something that even the world's largest technology companies have struggled to accomplish: Manufacture advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips at an unprecedented scale. Surprisingly, Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) could emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries of this vision.

Musk's Terafab project brings together Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) in an effort to reduce outside dependence on semiconductor manufacturing. For a company trying to turn around its foundry leadership, investors may be underestimating how this could transform Intel in the AI infrastructure era.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

What is Terafab?

Terafab is a proposed semiconductor manufacturing facility in Grimes County, Texas. So far, Tesla and SpaceX have committed initial investments of $16.8 billion for the first phase of the project. Terfab's goal is to stitch together chip design, advanced logic and memory manufacturing, and semiconductor packaging within a vertically integrated operation.

Musk's long-term goal is to produce enough annual chip production to support 1 terawatt of computing power. Terafab aims to produce two categories of processors. The first will power Tesla's autonomous vehicles, Optimus humanoid robots, and other AI applications operating here on Earth. The second is meant to support SpaceX's plans for space-based data centers.

Intel could be the hidden winner of Terafab

In April, Intel's participation in Terafab was confirmed, positioning its manufacturing expertise and advanced semiconductor technologies alongside Musk's grand plans. The company has been developing its 18A and 14A manufacturing processes, which are central to its effort to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing 's leading foundry capabilities.

Intel's foundry business stands to benefit enormously from securing a high-profile customer with substantial long-term chip requirements. More importantly, there is already some encouraging evidence of improving execution.

During the second quarter, Intel Foundry generated $5.8 billion in revenue, although most of that came from manufacturing chips for Intel's own products. External foundry revenue was only $293 million, and the division reported an operating loss of approximately $2.1 billion as a whole.

Story Continues

This is why Terafab matters so much. If Intel can prove that its technology meets Musk's requirements, it could strengthen credibility with other AI chip designers. Given the nascent nature of the project, Intel's potential manufacturing volumes and financial impact remain highly uncertain. Nevertheless, the company possesses something valuable: an opportunity to demonstrate that its foundry technology belongs in the same conversation alongside other industry leaders.

Is Intel stock a buy?

Terafab represents something different for various companies. For Tesla and SpaceX, it could reduce dependence on outside chip suppliers and support AI-driven growth across autonomous driving and robotics. For Nvidia, it introduces another potential source of competition as more companies develop custom silicon.

For Intel, the implications could be transformational. Intel does not need to displace Nvidia as the leading AI accelerator designer. Rather, the company is positioned to profit by helping other companies manufacture their chips. This is an attractive position to be in during an era when AI infrastructure spending continues to accelerate.

Still, in the long run, Intel will have to improve manufacturing yields, control capital expenditures (capex), attract additional external customers, and eventually turn its foundry operations profitable. Working on Terafab alone won't accomplish these objectives collectively.

For now, I see Intel stock as a speculative buy for investors comfortable with execution risk, understanding Terafab's eventual financial contribution remains uncertain. The bigger thesis is that Intel could become an attractive alternative to Taiwan Semi as demand for advanced AI chip manufacturing grows.

news.Title: Prediction: A $1,000 Investment in TSMC Stock Will More Than Double by 2030. Here’s Why You Should Buy It Before Oct. 15.
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), popularly known as TSMC, has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global chip boom, primarily due to its position as the largest semiconductor foundry that manufactures chips for major consumer electronics companies and chip designers that serve multiple end markets.

TSMC has capitalized on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom in recent years, thanks mainly to its advanced process nodes, which enable customers to manufacture cutting-edge chips. Not surprisingly, TSMC stock has gained nearly 384% over the past three years, outperforming the 246% gain in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the same period.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I won't be surprised to see this semiconductor stock head higher after it releases its third-quarter results on Oct. 15. Let's look at the reasons why TSMC is primed for more upside, potentially doubling by 2030.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

TSMC's accelerating growth suggests that its bull run is far from over

This has been a strong year for TSMC. The company's revenue has increased by 41% in the first nine months of 2026, suggesting it is on track to exceed its 2025 revenue growth of 36%.

Notably, TSMC's revenue growth has accelerated in recent months. Its September revenue increased nearly 55% from the same month in 2025, while August 2026 revenue was up by 53% over the same month last year. TSMC's Q3 revenue increased by 50% from the same period last year to $46.71 billion, beating estimates and exceeding the company's guidance range of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion.

What's more, the company's net profit is expected to increase by 64% from the year-ago period, as noted by Reuters . In fact, Reuters points out that TSMC is on track to report its sixth consecutive quarter of record profits due to the huge investments in AI infrastructure. The good part is that the AI infrastructure boom is far from over.

Nvidia , for instance, expects to double its chip sales next year. On the other hand, Advanced Micro Devices expects it can substantially boost supply in 2027, as it sees strong demand for advanced chips driven by AI. Both Nvidia and AMD are TSMC's customers.

As a result, it is easy to see why TSMC is reportedly planning to increase the production capacity of its advanced chip nodes next year. Market research firm TrendForce reports that TSMC's 2-nanometer (nm) chip production capacity could jump 22% by mid-2027 compared to the end of 2026. Additionally, the semiconductor giant is reportedly planning a 16% increase in 3nm production capacity over the same period.

Story Continues

TSMC gets a third of its revenue from these two process nodes, so higher production bodes well for the company's performance next year. Also, TSMC is reportedly set to increase prices for its advanced nodes by 5%-10% next year, according to Taiwan's national news agency.

So, TSMC should ideally witness a strong increase in both volumes and margins in 2027, which should allow it to sustain its robust revenue and earnings growth. Moreover, I won't be surprised to see TSMC offer a stronger-than-expected outlook when it reports results on Oct. 15, as AI customers such as Nvidia and AMD build up inventory to meet strong end-market demand.

TSMC's sunny guidance could pave the way for more upside. Moreover, TSMC increased its global semiconductor revenue forecast for 2030 to $1.5 trillion in May this year, up from the earlier estimate of $1 trillion. So, the strong jump in TSMC's revenue and earnings is sustainable beyond 2027, and that's what analysts are expecting.

TSM Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

A $1,000 investment in TSMC stock is going to be a smart move

If you have $1,000 in investible cash after meeting your expenses, saving for tough times, and clearing expensive loans, you can consider buying this AI stock with that money. The reason why I say this is that analysts have become quite bullish about TSMC's earnings growth prospects this year.

TSM EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

Specifically, TSMC's earnings are anticipated to increase by 60% in 2026 to $17.04 per share. The forecast for the next couple of years points to solid 30% increases.

TSM EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Assuming TSMC's bottom line increases by even 20% in 2029 and 2030, its earnings per share could hit $42.05 by the end of the decade. If TSMC trades at 30 times earnings at that time, a slight discount to the Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple of 31.5, its stock price could reach $1,261. That's 184% higher than where TSMC stock is right now.

So, a $1,000 investment in TSMC could be worth more than $2,800 in 2030, which is why investors should consider buying this multibagger stock before it soars higher following its Oct. 15 report.

news.Title: Should You Sell Tesla? I Sold 1 Other Winner Too Early. Here's What I Learned.
news.Content:
Shares of electric vehicle (EV) titan Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) are enjoying a surge in October. The company reported third-quarter vehicle delivery numbers ahead of Wall Street's estimates on Oct. 2, creating anticipation for promising earnings when the company announces Q3 results on Oct. 21. The stock closed at $382.70 on Oct. 9, up nearly 8% from the end of September.

However, shares are still down about 13% during the past 12 months. Given the October bump, is now the time to sell Tesla stock?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I advise against it. I sold shares in another company after they experienced a spike back in 2021, and I regret it. That stock was Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and it's a cautionary tale about the importance of adhering to a key Motley Fool investing philosophy: Let your winners keep winning.

My Meta mistake

In 2021, the world was suffering through the COVID-19 pandemic. People were staying home and spending large amounts of time online. This increased consumer traffic to Meta's web properties, causing shares of the social media giant to skyrocket to $382.18 on Sept. 7 of that year, a record closing price at the time.

That was quite the rise from its initial public offering price of $38 in 2012, the year I bought shares. The stock was a clear winner. However, I thought the pandemic-induced share price increase wouldn't last after society returned to normal. I was also dubious of Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg's plans for the metaverse, which he introduced in 2021. These factors drove me to sell.

In the short term, I was right. Meta's foray into the metaverse floundered, as its Reality Labs division lost $13.7 billion in 2022. The company's forecasts for user and revenue growth that year failed to materialize, and the stock fell.

Winners keep winning

Then, artificial intelligence (AI) arrived. Zuckerberg quickly pivoted Meta toward heavy investments in AI. The recent release of its Muse AI app was a hit, garnering 2 million daily users. Meta stock closed at $718.67 on Oct. 9, about double where I sold.

As Motley Fool co-founder David Gardner has stated , "Past performance may well be the single best indicator you and I have of future results. What do winners do? Winners win."

I forgot that valuable piece of advice. I may have gotten around a 10-fold return on Meta, which is awesome, but I missed out on shares that soared 88% from there, not to mention the passive income after Meta began paying a dividend in 2024.

Story Continues

All of that taught me you don't want to get rid of your winners. Tesla is one of those. It's quickly evolving beyond its electric-vehicle roots and leveraging AI as a key element in that evolution. In fact, famed Wall Street analyst Dan Ives believes it should not be evaluated as a car company, stating, "We view Tesla as one of the clearest ways to own physical AI in the public markets."

Why Tesla stock is worth holding

Tesla has been working on AI for more than a decade. This culminated in the launch of its autonomous ride-hailing business using the new Cybercab on Sept. 3, creating a new revenue stream. A month later, the company announced that more than 300 of these self-driving vehicles now serve Austin, Texas, an eightfold increase. The fast ramp-up indicates the Cybercab is gaining customer traction.

Capitalizing on AI is just the start. Tesla's vision for the future is a world of "sustainable abundance." This concept entails using technology sustainably to create boundless prosperity for all. This ambitious target highlights the company's commitment to tackling challenges once considered impossible, much like its early efforts to build a viable electric vehicle.

Today, it has succeeded in EVs. While its electric auto sales in the second quarter rose 23% year over year to $20.5 billion, rival Ford Motor Company experienced a huge 56% drop in Q2 EV revenue to $1 billion. Tesla's Q3 delivery numbers suggest more growth ahead.

The company's strong sales despite last year's expiration of federal EV tax credits, the Cybercab showing early success, and a far-flung vision for the future are some of the reasons I'm holding my Tesla shares. It could end up being the winning stock you were glad you didn't sell too early.

news.Title: 晶片股拋售潮席捲亞洲 韓股暴跌觸發暫停交易 亞股周二全線收低
news.Content:
亞太股市周二(13日)劇烈震盪，MSCI亞太(日本除外)指數大跌逾2%，摔至今年7月下旬以來新低。隨前一晚美國費城半導體指數(SOX-US)下跌2.7%，市場對人工智慧(AI)供應鏈龐大資本支出的獲利能力產生疑慮，引發全球晶片與科技股大規模拋售潮，重創亞洲主要股市。

在消息面上，市場傳出中國記憶體大廠長鑫存儲(CXMT)在DRAM架構取得突破，晶胞面積縮減約30%並計畫於2026年底推出新產品。這引發投資人擔憂中國業者加速縮小技術差距，未來記憶體市場恐面臨競爭加劇與過剩風險，直接衝擊美韓晶片巨頭的溢價優勢。

同時，市場開始檢視AI企業的資本投入報酬率與實際獲利能力。加上美國10年期公債殖利率仍在高點5.2%附近、布蘭特原油價格維持在每桶106美元高檔以及美元走強，高利率環境使資金成本顯著上升，壓抑風險資產評價。

南韓(KOSPI指數)成為周二受創最深的主力市場，指數盤中重挫逾7%，一度跌破6,000點大關，終場大跌5.46%，收6,035.35點。由於波動過於劇烈，南韓交易所一度啟動5分鐘的單側熔斷(Sidecar)機制，為近兩個月來首次。市值占比極高的記憶體雙雄三星電子與SK海力士分別重挫7.4%與10%，均為連續第5個交易日下跌。

日本日經指數下挫近2%。其中記憶體大廠鎧俠(Kioxia)暴跌逾13%，科技投資巨頭軟銀(SoftBank)重挫超8%。亞洲晶片股賣壓同步遞延至歐美市場，那斯達克期貨跌幅在0.6%至1%之間，歐洲股市期貨下滑0.2%至0.4%。

分析師指出，半導體產業仍具周期性特徵，後續市場焦點將轉向即將公布的美國大型銀行財報、美國CPI通膨數據，以及ASML與台積電等半導體龍頭的最新法說會展望，藉此評估AI資本支出動能與全球資金走向。

news.Title: Global chip selloff deepens as AI worries, China competition weigh
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Shares of U.S. and European chipmakers fell Tuesday as a selloff in AI-exposed stocks deepened, pulling the broader technology sector lower amid concerns over the sustainability of AI investment and intensifying competition.

In U.S. premarket trading, Micron fell 2.3%, with Marvell Technology and SanDisk also sliding more than 2% by 04:28 ET (08:28 GMT). Western Digital dropped nearly 4%, and AMD and Broadcom each fell about 1%.

Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »

European chip names were hit harder. STMicroelectronics dipped 2.6%, Soitec and Infineon fell more than 1%, while chip-testing company Technoprobe slid 2.6%. Siltronic slipped 1.4%, Aixtron fell 1.9%, and ASM International lost 2.4%. Among equipment makers, ASML and BE Semiconductor shed over 1% each.

The moves followed a steep drop in Asian memory stocks. SK Hynix plunged 10%, Samsung Electronics lost 7.4%, and Tokyo-listed Kioxia fell as much as 13.3%. In Japan, SoftBank Group, which has significant exposure to the global AI industry, sank 8.5% and led a broader retreat in the country's semiconductor and electronics shares.

Those declines came after a weak session for tech on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.44% Monday. Micron slid 3.9% as investors weighed rising competition from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies. Over the weekend, CXMT said it had made significant progress on a new chip architecture designed to increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space.

news.Title: 《韓股》半導體賣壓拖累 KOSPI收跌5.46%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-13 16:43:12 數位內容中心 發佈

韓股今(13)日明顯轉弱，韓國KOSPI指數收於6035.35點，下跌348.89點或5.46%；韓國KOSDAQ指數收於837.03點，下跌12.16點或1.43%。盤中賣壓一度使KOSPI指數跌至6000點下方，尾盤雖勉強收復整數關卡，但整體基調仍是急跌與避險升溫。

外部環境方面，市場壓力主要來自風險趨避情緒升高，外資賣超成為壓低指數的主要力量，韓元兌美元同步走弱，也放大了資金撤離的氣氛。盤中波動急劇放大，KOSPI指數早盤還觸發「sell sidecar」，顯示市場對下行風險已明顯敏感。

半導體權值股方面，跌勢最重的是晶片族群，Samsung Electronics(005930.KS)與SK hynix(000660.KS)走弱，成為KOSPI指數回檔的主要拖累。市場解讀，長鑫存儲(CXMT)傳出DRAM技術進展並擬推出新產品後，韓國記憶體股承受直接壓力，AI估值疑慮與中國晶片競爭升溫也進一步打擊信心。

類股與個股方面，在權值股領跌下，KOSPI指數相關大型科技股同步承壓，KOSDAQ指數雖然跌幅較小，但也無法獨善其身。市場沒有出現明顯的防禦性轉強，顯示賣壓並非只集中在單一個股，而是延伸到整體科技資產與高估值族群。

news.Title: 《日股》AI賣壓拖累 日經收跌1.82%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-13 16:33:28 數位內容中心 發佈

日股今(13)日走勢分歧，日經225指數收於67,777.52點，下跌1,253.40點或1.82%；東證股價指數(TOPIX)收於4,110.67點，上漲5.86點或0.14%。市場主軸仍是AI與半導體相關股遭到拋售，日經指數盤中跌幅一度逼近2,000點，尾盤雖略有收斂，但仍明顯承壓，顯示權值科技股的走弱是今日盤面核心。

科技權值股方面，前一交易日美國半導體股走弱，壓力迅速傳導至日股。東京威力科創(8035.JP)、愛德萬測試(6857.JP)、軟銀集團(9984.JP)、Kioxia Holdings(285A.JP)、Lasertec(6920.JP)、TDK(6762.JP)、Murata Manufacturing(6981.JP)等個股多數下跌，成為日經指數回檔主因；相較之下，Fast Retailing(9983.JP)、Recruit Holdings(6098.JP)、FANUC(6954.JP)等則走強，對大盤跌勢提供一定緩衝。

類股方面，盤面資金並未全面撤離，而是明顯轉向海運、石油與煤炭製品、銀行與保險等類股，商船三井(9104.JP)等航運股表現突出；相較之下，非鐵金屬、電機設備、資訊與通信等類股偏弱，顯示市場在AI與半導體估值回檔之際，資金改抱較具防禦與循環特性的族群。

外部變數方面，中東情勢不明與原油價格偏強，讓能源成本與通膨壓力的疑慮升高，進一步壓抑風險偏好。市場也關注AI大型投資能否轉化為實際獲利，以及半導體需求是否持續，這些因素持續左右資金對高估值成長股的態度。

news.Title: 台股收跌960點！ 金融、台塑四寶逆勢揚 「這檔千金」創新高
news.Content:
受美國費城半導體指數連四挫及科技股賣壓籠罩影響，台股今（13）日多頭重挫。加權指數開低走低，盤中一度大跌逾1,200點、失守49,000點大關，終場重挫960.65點，收在48,341.31點，跌幅1.95%，回測月線尋求支撐，成交量1.12兆元。

電子權值股成為今日賣壓重災區，台積電（2330）因法說會前夕遭遇外資提款，重挫50元至2490元，跌幅1.97%，聯發科（2454）、台達電（2308）等權值大將也連袂壓低，聯發科下跌100元，來到4525元，跌幅2.16%，台達電下跌125元，來到1775元跌幅6.58%。鴻海下跌4.50元，來到240.00元，跌幅1.84%。

然而，盤面資金迅速轉向避險與傳產族群，台塑四寶營運回溫展現抗跌韌性，台塑化（6505）受惠油價與利差擴大，盤中爆量急衝亮燈漲停，南亞（1303）漲幅逾5%，台塑（1301）、台化（1326）也有1%左右的漲幅。金融股亦扮演關鍵撐盤角色的重要支柱，富邦金（2881）強勢走揚，盤中最高來到161.5元，華南金（2880）盤中更飆漲逾3%衝上49.6元，雙雙刷新歷史新高紀錄。

此外，光學廠玉晶光（3406）亮燈創新天價，上漲105元，來到1175元，漲幅9.81%。被動元件族群也逆勢上漲，天二科技（6834）亮燈漲停，上漲14.5元，來到159.5元，漲幅10%。

news.Title: 【台股盤後】挫960點科技股賣壓沉重　塑化、航運與金融強勢
news.Content:
（中央社記者曾仁凱台北2026年10月13日電）博通執行長陳福陽、英特爾執行長陳立武雙雙示警，AI擴張最大瓶頸已非晶片，而是資金，引爆科技股賣壓，週一美國費城半導體指數連4黑，日、韓股今天也走弱，拖累台股今天盤中最多重跌逾1200點，回測48000點關卡。

終場集中市場指數下跌960.65點，收在48341.31點，成交值放大到新台幣1兆1250億元。

3大權值股方面，台積電 (2330) 今天收盤下跌50元或1.97%，收在2490元，聯發科 (2454) 跌100元或2.16%，收在4525元，台達電 (2308) 跌125元或6.58%，收1775元。

金融股成為撐盤要角，華南金 (2880) 大漲1.7元或3.57%，收49.35元；中信金 (2891) 、第一金 (2892) 收盤漲幅都超過2%。

台塑四寶昨天公布第3季自結財報，南亞 (1303) 、台塑化 (6505) 單季獲利創新高，外加油價上漲助攻，激勵塑化族群。台塑化今天收盤攻上漲停板119元，南亞大漲超過半根停板，二線塑化股，國喬 (1312) 亮燈漲停，東聯 (1710) 漲逾8%。

資深分析師蔡明翰分析，美國費城半導體今年以來漲幅大，最近出現比較明顯的拉回走勢，尤其在台灣國慶連假期間連續下跌。台股昨天連假後首日開低走高，展現抗跌力道，但該反映的還是得反映，今天台股下跌，日、韓股同樣偏弱。

不過蔡明翰觀察，這波費半指數回檔，美股主要指數走勢並非同步，如美國道瓊工業昨天上漲，顯示投資人並未恐慌，而且市場也沒有出現太特別的利空，族群輪動是好現象；本週頭號重點還是觀察週四即將登場的台積電法說會。

news.Title: 搭上三星與K-Pop ！「純韓股 ETF」009829遭韓股血洗慘跌7％
news.Content:
亞股今（13）日血洗！韓股跳水大跌逾6%，科技巨頭首當其衝，三星電子跌近7%，SK 海力士更殺近一成。作為全台唯一高純度涵蓋韓國前五十名市值龍頭的 ETF—大華韓國 KOSPI 50（009829），雖然精準卡位半導體記憶體霸主，並搭上韓流 K-Pop、韓國網漫與三星供應鏈等高成長題材，可惜生不逢時，今（13）日又遇到市場亂流。盤中一度重摔 7.59%；儘管尾盤跌勢略有收斂，終場仍大跌 6.81%，收在 9.58 元。

隨著市場焦點鎖定的三星電子第3季初步業績法說會，南韓股市（KOSPI）展開強烈攻防。009829經理人賴昱廷表示，儘管短線受韓元走升及美債殖利率波動影響，但南韓半導體出口暴增趨勢不變，對半導體龍頭的結構性需求依然堅堅挺。

在AI半導體與財報前景方面，賴昱廷表示，三星電子與SK海力士受惠於AI伺服器對HBM4與高階DRAM的強勁拉貨，記憶體庫存仍處於10天以下的極低狀態。雖然匯率波動帶來短線獲利調整疑慮，但AI記憶體供需失衡的結構性趨勢未變，市場預期三星電子法說會將釋出亮眼的HBM供應進展與資本支出展望，為晶片類股重奪KOSPI指數領頭羊地位提供有力支撐。

賴昱廷強調，009829（大華韓國KOSPI50）前兩大持股SK海力士（33.88%）、三星電子（31.24%）直接受惠於AI晶片超級週期與財報利多；同時囊括現代汽車、KB金融等受益於企業價值提升政策的低P/E高股息標的，以及引領全球流行文化輸出的娛樂消費與數位內容龍頭。在AI算力需求持續告急、政策改革與K-Culture全球紅利同步發酵的背景下，建議投資人不妨透過009829布局南韓龍頭企業，跨國資金重估趨勢下，作為資產配置效益的核心選擇。

但賴昱廷也提醒，市場仍受總體經濟及國際政經變化干擾，投資人應評估自身風險承受度，以單筆分批或定期定額方式進行中長期規劃。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 韓股血崩7％不只記憶體開槍！還有2大隱形殺手 大老竟爆市場像在「賭場」
news.Content:
韓國股市今（13）日盤中一度崩跌7%，兩大指標權值股三星電子與 SK 海力士股價重挫7%至 8%，短短 4個交易日大盤累計暴跌15%。韓股10月2日收在 7003 點，今日最低下探5911 點，一度摜破年線5990點，距離7月底股災低點5262點僅剩約一成距離。若跌勢持續，本周不排除見到前波低點。

綜合外媒報導，南韓曾是全球熱門的AI交易市場之一。在AI熱潮推動下，記憶體晶片利潤飆升，槓桿散戶與海外資金集中湧入，KOSPI指數上半年一度上漲約一倍。然而進入下半年，行情迅速反轉，指數下挫 22%，成為同期表現最差的市場之一；然而美股卻持續走高。

權重過度集中半導體 投機資金退潮爆賣壓

Bloomberg Markets Live策略師指出，這場反轉並不代表AI基礎設施需求崩潰，核心問題在於南韓股市過度依賴少數半導體巨頭。當投機資金退潮後，市場缺乏足夠買盤承接拋售賣壓。

博通執行長陳福陽日前警告，資金緊縮可能成爲比晶片短缺最大的瓶頸。他於新加坡一場公開活動中指出，許多投資人並不清楚自身的投資標的，設定了非常極端的期望，這讓市場操作幾乎就像在賭場一樣。

與此同時，大陸記憶體指標廠長鑫科技近期宣布在4F² DRAM架構研發取得關鍵突破，預計年底推出結合 4F² 與混合鍵合（Hybrid Bonding）技術的新一代 DDR5 RDIMM 伺服器記憶體。若新產品順利通過客戶認證，將顯著拉升長鑫在伺服器記憶體的市場版圖。

55兆韓元庫藏股支撐消失 外資持續撤離韓股

Pepperstone 集團研究策略師Dilin Wu指出，三星與SK海力士在KOSPI指數的權重極高，全球市場對AI行情的所有疑慮，都會在首爾股市被大幅放大。另一方面，長鑫科技的技術突破，也直接踩中投資人關注的核心問題，即南韓記憶體巨頭的競爭優勢究竟還能維持多久？

南韓股市總市值約 4.3 兆美元，三星與 SK 海力士合計佔KOSPI權重超過一半，使指數高度依賴記憶體產業的盈利前景與市場情緒。

另一項利空在於兩家公司的股票回購計畫接近尾聲。三星與SK海力士回購規模合計55兆韓元（約 4100億美元）。摩根大通估計，兩家公司回購貢獻了上月南韓股市買盤的大部分動力。隨著護盤資金退場，市場急需尋找新資金承接股票。但在

但在外資持續撤離、散戶降低槓桿的情況下，即便企業獲利維持成長，缺乏新資金流入也難以推升股價迅速反彈。

news.Title: 台股收盤重挫960點！台積電暴跌50元 3大族群苦撐紅盤
news.Content:
台股今（13日）開低走低，盤中一度大跌1235點，隨後跌勢略為收斂，終場下跌960.65點收在48341.31點，成交量1.12兆元。權值股台積電跌50元收在2490元，台達電挫低125元收在1775元，聯發科也下跌100元收在4525元，電子股成為重災區，光通訊、記憶體、矽晶圓、被動元件、CCL及PCB等熱門族群皆被擊落，僅傳產航運塑化與金融族群收紅。

近期美股高估值族群出現回檔，費城半導體指數成為重災區，加上國際油價上漲，通膨疑慮再起，使人工智慧產業的利空與質疑又被放大，美股下殺後台日韓股市也急跌，日股跌逾2%，韓股重挫逾6%。

摩爾投顧分析師林漢偉指，台股面臨補跌壓力，美股科技股連續回檔，費半指數重挫2.67%，台積電ADR跌破月線，加上外資持續提款，電子權值股面臨賣壓。資金轉向塑化、航運，中小型股則以個股表現為主。

林漢偉建議投資人多看少做，控制資金水位，嚴防外資提款壓力，電子權值股面臨賣壓，中小型股則會轉為個股表現的游擊戰，「台股補跌回測十日線壓力沉重，應汰弱留強不亂搶反彈，避開位階偏高的電子股，把資金轉進具備實質受惠油價的塑化族群，或者9月營收亮眼的個股，保持耐心度過亂流。」

法人認為，投資人後市需要觀察3大止跌訊號，包括匯率走勢、法人籌碼及技術面表現，外資是否重站買方、新台幣是否大幅升值帶動資金回流，或者出現帶量的紅K棒及長下影線。

news.Title: Better Artificial Intelligence Stock for 2026: Intel vs. NVIDIA
news.Content:
The semiconductor landscape is shifting as traditional leaders and new giants battle for dominance in the artificial intelligence era. Choosing between Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) requires weighing a massive turnaround effort against explosive growth.

Intel is attempting to reinvent itself as a world-class chip manufacturer while maintaining its legacy PC and server presence. NVIDIA remains the undisputed leader in graphics processing units (GPUs) that power modern data centers. Comparing these two helps investors decide if they prefer a high-margin growth leader or a value-driven recovery story.

The case for Intel

Intel is a veteran among semiconductor stocks , focusing on designing and manufacturing semiconductors through various business divisions, such as its data center and foundry segments. The company maintains a strategic partnership with Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) to develop next-generation AI chipmaking capabilities. This foundry strategy aims to build chips for other companies, though expanding this infrastructure requires significant capital.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue reached $52.9 billion, representing a slight decline of 0.5% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company reported a net loss of $267.0 million, resulting in a negative net margin of 0.5%. This performance reflects the ongoing costs of its transition and competitive pressures in its core markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.4x, while the current ratio, measuring the ability to pay short-term obligations, was 2.0x. Free cash flow was negative at $4.9 billion, which is calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 25.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for NVIDIA

NVIDIA dominates the market for hardware that powers accelerated computing and artificial intelligence. The company serves massive cloud service providers and has a long-standing agreement with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT). It is also strengthening its technology through deals such as its "acqui-hire" of Groq, which focuses on specialized chips for language model inference, with Nvidia hiring Groq's founder and other key members of the team.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 25, 2026, revenue reached $215.9 billion, a surge of 65.5% over the previous year. This growth drove net income to $120.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of 55.6%. These figures highlight the massive demand for its chips across global data centers and enterprise AI deployments.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, NVIDIA maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. Its current ratio stood at 3.9x, indicating a strong position to cover near-term liabilities. Free cash flow reached $96.7 billion.

Risk profile comparison

Intel faces significant competitive threats within the semiconductor industry, particularly as rivals move faster in AI innovation. The company also deals with ongoing regulatory scrutiny and risks related to protecting its intellectual property. Furthermore, potential volatility in market demand for its products could disrupt its long-term manufacturing turnaround plans.

NVIDIA deals with high revenue concentration, as a limited number of partners and customers account for a large portion of its sales. It faces legal challenges, including securities class actions and regulatory hurdles regarding its $20 billion deal with Groq, which was challenged because it effectively transferred Groq's core technology and key engineering talent to NVIDIA without the transaction being treated as an acquisition. Geopolitical risks in regions like Taiwan and strict U.S. export controls also limit its ability to sell into certain international markets.

Valuation comparison

NVIDIA carries a lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates, though it maintains a higher P/S ratio based on sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

NVIDIA and Intel are key players in the burgeoning AI market, making both ideal companies to invest in. That said, between the two, I would choose NVIDIA over Intel.

Intel stock has soared more than 180% in the past 12 months through Oct. 12, while NVIDIA is up about 25% in that time. However, a year ago, Intel had a lot to prove after struggling to benefit from the AI boom.

That's why Intel's fiscal 2025 sales of $52.9 billion represented a year-over-year decline. Its stock jumped as new CEO Lip-Bu Tan began to deliver on turnaround efforts. The company's $16.1 billion in its fiscal Q2, ended June 27, was a substantial 25% year-over-year revenue increase.

NVIDIA's stock has not risen as much as Intel's, and given its much lower forward earnings multiple, shares are a better value. The company added a massive $150 billion to its existing share repurchase program in a sign it believes its stock is undervalued.

But what makes NVIDIA the stock to buy is its dominant position in the AI ecosystem. The semiconductor giant doesn't just sell GPUs essential to AI systems. Its CUDA software platform is integral to optimizing GPUs for AI, making switching costs high for customers.

Building on this, NVIDIA acquired Hugging Face, a platform for developers to construct open AI models. This move positions the company as a key player in assisting the AI economy to flourish.

news.Title: AI「錢荒」來了？美股AI拋售潮外溢  韓股早盤挫7%熔斷、日股跌超3%  鎧陜崩逾13%
news.Content:
一場由美股AI硬體股引發的拋售潮週二(13日)蔓延至亞洲，韓股早盤跌逾7%、摜破6000點，觸發SIDECAR暫停KOSPI程式賣盤，三星電子跌超8%、SK海力士跌超9%，日股也在同日補跌，日經225跌超3%、一度挫逾1700點，鎧俠早盤崩跌13.2%、軟銀跌8.2%。MSCI亞太指數亦創逾兩個月低，A股創業板早盤跌逾3%，香港恒生科技跌超2%，算力硬體、半導體、大型科技股齊挫。

Lumentum在美股週一(12日)跌近10%，康寧、閃迪跌約6%，美光、希捷跌超3%，安謀、SK海力士跌超4%，甲骨文跌近3%，輝達跌超1%。

英特爾、博通執行長近日直言，AI擴張最大瓶頸已非晶片而是資金，雲廠資本開支續增，但自由現金流承壓，長天期美債利率偏高推升資料中心融資成本。市場對「需求永動機」敘事重新定價，轉向檢視資本開支可持續性與投資回報。

橋水創辦人達利歐在新加坡福布斯全球CEO大會警告，AI投資熱已是「經典泡沫」，受債務融資與利率上行驅動，距破裂臨界點「已很近」。

分析人士認為，長線算力需求未消失，但高估值正接受融資成本與現金流壓力考驗，亞洲半導體權重股短期波動恐延續。縱觀全球AI行情，本輪調整的本質是市場對AI敘事的一次集中重定價。過去一年全球科技股的定價核心邏輯是「算力即權力」，但隨著AI資本開支規模不斷擴大，市場開始追問一個更現實的問題：這筆錢從哪裡來？

短期來看，恐慌情緒仍在跨市場傳導，高估值科技股與利率敏感的半導體族群仍將面臨波動壓力。

不過，市場認為，AI基本面未徹底反轉，算力長期需求邏輯沒有消失，變動的是估價定價邏輯。

news.Title: 《日股早盤》AI與半導體走弱 日經指數下跌2.5%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-13 10:35:41 黃文章 發佈

日經指數週二早盤下跌，受到前一交易日美國半導體類股下跌影響，人工智慧（AI）與半導體相關股票幾乎全面走低。軟銀集團（SoftBank Group）股價下跌8.5%，也成為拖累日經平均指數走勢的因素。

日經225指數13日早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)下跌2.52%或1,738.53點，暫收67,292.39點。東證股價指數(TOPIX)早盤收盤下跌0.46%或18.90點，暫收4,085.91點。

就類股表現來看，截至早盤收盤為止，海運業（2.66%）、證券業（2.00%）漲幅較大，跌幅較大的類股為非鐵金屬（-4.52%）、電氣機器（-3.21%）。

一名日本國內證券公司的策略師表示：「若要讓日經平均指數在7萬點站穩，其中一項必要條件，是觀察10月下半月起正式展開的4月至9月期財報發布，確認AI與半導體相關產業的需求是否持續擴大。」

另一方面，由於中東局勢日益緊張，原油價格維持在高檔，帶動能源類股受到買盤青睞。此外，市場預期通膨加速可能推升未來利率，銀行、保險等有利於利率上升的金融類股也隨之走高。
