news.Title: 群益投信Q4投資展望，聚焦「DUO」策略，兼顧成長收益
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者劉居全報導】今年第三季雖受通膨升溫、AI變現疑慮影響，全球金融市場呈現高檔震盪，但整體經濟展現韌性，基本面、企業獲利與資金動能同步增強，評價面經過回檔修正後回到合理區間，為後續行情奠定基礎。展望第四季，群益投信表示，利率變化仍將牽動市場風險偏好，但隨AI應用加速擴散、企業營運續旺，多頭格局可望延續，短期波動反而提供重新檢視與布局的契機。面對機會與挑戰並存的環境，投資人可採用「DUO」高效投資策略，以多工處理（Multi-tasking）的理財思維進行股債多元配置，掌握科技趨勢與成長契機，同時建立收益與防禦機制，靈活因應市場變化，打造攻守兼備的投資組合，在震盪中穩健前行。群益投信指出，「DUO」高效投資策略中的「D」代表Diversify多元分散風險，今年來全球金融市場震盪頻繁，穩健型投資人可透過「先固息、後增益」架構，利用多重資產基金、目標風險組合平衡基金，或結合具有高息優勢的債券基金及ETF，像是金融債基金、非投等債基金、優先順位非投等債基金、短天期ESG BBB級投等債ETF、優選非投等債ETF等，以獲得穩建息收並降低投組波動。「U」為Upside Trend 掌握上行趨勢，在AI需求強勁與應用落地，以及大廠資本支出加速下，台美科技供應鏈獲利維持高成長，成為推升台股、美股向上的核心動能。投資人可透過主動式台股ETF、台股基金、主動式美股ETF、市值型美股ETF、科技型美股ETF、美國成長股基金，以參與AI核心商機。

群益投信進一步說明，「O」則是Opportunity捕捉潛力機會，尤其印度受惠於政策利多、內需強勁，有利股市重返成長格局，有意參與補漲行情的投資人可適度配置印度相關股票基金。此外，日本自首相高市早苗上任後，積極推動各項改革政策，並邁向利率正常化，為日本經濟注入新動能。看好日股紅利的投資人，不妨透過以日股為核心部位的亞股基金來掌握新多頭行情。整體來看，「DUO」高效投資策略協助投資人抵禦波動，同時掌握潛在商機，以從容應對重啟升息後的經濟新局，同時達成資產穩健增值的理財目標。

升息短空長多，首選科技成長股、大型股、新興亞股、短債，兼顧成長收益

群益環球金綻雙喜基金經理人許書銘表示，中東戰事推升油價並加劇通膨壓力，促使聯準會重啟升息，主要央行也轉趨鷹派，全球進入高利率維持更久的新局面。不過歷史經驗顯示，升息對股市影響往往呈現「短空長多」，尤其在AI投資週期加速下，全球製造業PMI持續擴張，有助企業營運改善。預期企業獲利的強勁表現可望支撐升息初期的估值修正，待市場消化政策衝擊後，投資焦點仍將回到基本面。

許書銘進一步指出，面對經濟發展穩健、貨幣政策轉向的環境，第四季操作仍以股優於債為主，在股市布局上，隨著AI資本支出加速，可鎖定獲利能見度最高的科技成長股、財務體質良好的大型股，以及受惠於半導體超級週期的新興亞股。債券配置上，因應利率環境變化，短債表現相對受惠，可善用具收益優勢的非投等債、新興債建立穩健現金流來源，並強化投組防禦力。

高利率環境疊加企業獲利加速，美股進入成長淘汰賽，科技硬體仍是投資主線

群益美國科技巨頭ETF（009824）經理人李晉含指出，雖然市場面臨升息與資金成本提高的挑戰，但企業獲利的強勁增長足以抵銷估值壓力，市場表現依然穩健，今年前三季標普500指數上漲11.8%，屢創新高，同時企業獲利持續上修，使未來12個月本益比從年初的22.2倍降至19.1倍，顯示整體評價仍屬合理。然而，隨著利率走高，市場將更嚴格檢視AI商業化進程、自由現金流與變現能力，市場將進入企業層級的成長淘汰賽。後續可關注債券殖利率、油價走勢，操作上也須留意第四季財測與市場廣度變化。產業布局上，在市場最為關切的AI領域，在模型突破、硬體擴建、資本回收與代理商業化同時發展下，市場注意力形成四層重疊，角度也自能否建成延伸至能否應用、收費並留下現金，現階段來看，市場對接下來最高成長預期仍集中於AI基礎設施，相關硬體獲利可望延續，料為資金匯集之處，非電族群則可留意包括金融、航太與能源，以掌握個股輪動下的投資契機。

群益亞太新趨勢平衡基金經理人楊慈珍認為，受惠於全球AI需求殷切，亞洲科技產品出口與資本支出顯著增加，帶動區域今、明兩年GDP年增率上看4.8%、4.7%。雖然地緣政治風險加重通膨壓力，但部分亞太國家已啟動升息並逐步接近本輪利率目標，加上各國推行緩和物價政策，預估後續升息空間有限。從估值來看，目前MSCI亞太不含日本指數本益比僅10.5倍，明顯低於歐美股市，兼具評價優勢與長線投資價值。產業面來看，AI應用拓展帶動AI硬體需求，後續看好具缺貨題材、訂單能見度高，且受惠AI長期成長趨勢的科技、工業、非必須消費產業。操作上可分批布局以待行情發動，同時密切追蹤總經動能以及企業財報變化，以利汰弱留強。

群益馬拉松基金暨主動群益台灣強棒ETF（00982A）經理人陳沅易分析，儘管聯準會立場偏鷹、美債殖利率走升一度影響市場情緒，不過核心通膨逐步降溫、薪資與物價螺旋上升的風險亦低，長期利率壓力有望淡化。此外，待後續美國期中選舉結果出爐，政治、政策不確定性可望消退，市場焦點也將更回歸聚焦基本面。隨著AI應用需求大爆發，推升相關供應鏈獲利表現，預估今年台股企業獲利成長率上修至40%，明年將再成長25%，不僅進一步強化市場信心，也有助支持台股多頭延續。投資配置上，AI長期成長趨勢仍是核心主軸，可關注先進製程、先進封裝、廠務工程、矽光子、測試介面、PCB/CCL、ASIC及低軌衛星等獲利成長動能強勁族群，以掌握AI發展所帶來的成長紅利。

news.Title: TSMC Revenue Growth Accelerated Faster Than Expected Last Quarter. Here's Why It's My Top AI Chip Stock to Buy.
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) is the company behind the world's most advanced semiconductors. The largest third-party chip manufacturer has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of booming artificial intelligence (AI) spending, and that doesn't seem to be slowing down anytime soon.

TSMC's September revenue release showed accelerating sales growth, with the third quarter coming in above management's guidance and analysts' expectations. Here's what's driving the revenue growth for TSMC and why it's my top AI chip stock to buy.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

What's behind TSMC's rapid revenue growth?

TSMC reports monthly sales figures in New Taiwan dollars (NTD) shortly after the end of each month. September sales reached NT512 billion, up 55% year over year. Total third-quarter sales reached NT1.49 trillion, up 51%. However, the New Taiwan dollar lost value relative to the U.S. dollar over the past year, inflating those growth rates. Still, at an exchange rate of 32 NTD to USD, that translates into revenue of about $46.7 billion in revenue for the quarter, up 41% from a year ago and accelerating from 34% growth in Q2.

That number tops both analysts' expectations and TSMC's own internal forecast for revenue between $44.6 billion and $45.8 billion. Management also expected gross margin to come in between 65% and 67% and operating margin between 56% and 58%. Both represent contractions from Q2 but remain close to record levels for the company. We'll have to wait until next week for TSMC to reveal the full earnings results.

There are several significant factors driving TSMC's revenue growth.

First and foremost is the robust demand for AI-related chips. As mentioned, chipmakers rely on TSMC's manufacturing technology to develop the world's most advanced chips, which has led to booming demand for the company.

Second, TSMC quickly ramped up its 2-nanometer (2nm) production process last quarter. The technology accounted for just 3% of revenue in Q2, but that should climb quickly. While that could result in some margin pressure on the business, TSMC is reportedly charging premium pricing for its newest production node, which should offset much of it. What's more, a faster ramp means tooling utilization increases faster, reducing pressure on margins.

Story Continues

Beyond 2nm, pricing is well above existing processes, and management reportedly increased pricing at the start of the year for most of its chips. It plans to continue raising prices every year through at least 2029, with expectations to raise prices 10% at the start of next year.

The last piece of the revenue growth formula is TSMC's massive capacity increases. TSMC has spent heavily on capital expenditure (capex) to meet the demand of AI chip designers that contract with it. That's enabled it to bring more capacity online, and it's actually accelerated its 2nm capacity build-out for 2026. It has plans to spend hundreds of billions on new facilities in Arizona, and it's also exploring building in Texas to diversify from the geopolitical risk of its Asian facilities.

Here's why it's my top AI chip stock

What makes TSMC such a compelling investment is that it's built a wide moat that's enabled it to take market share from competitors despite already dominating the third-party chip manufacturing space. It's unlikely a company like Nvidia or Apple will be able to move a significant amount of work away from TSMC to negatively impact its growth at any point in the future. Nor is it likely they'll want to in the first place.

TSMC benefits from a virtuous cycle. As the world's largest chip fabricator, it generates a large amount of revenue relative to its peers. It can use that revenue to reinvest in research and development and additional capacity. That ensures its technology remains best in class, and it has the capacity to fulfill the growing number of orders from its chip design partners.

Importantly, TSMC is relatively agnostic about who designs the chips it makes. While Nvidia rules the roost today, it might not always be the biggest designer for AI chips. Custom silicon is growing in popularity among the hyperscalers. Regardless of who designs the chips, TSMC will be the company manufacturing them.

That gives me confidence in management's long-term revenue growth outlook of 25% average annualized sales growth between 2024 and 2029. Management is well ahead of that target, and CEO C.C. Wei suggested that number will increase once again when TSMC next updates its guidance.

With Taiwan Semiconductor stock trading for just 27 times earnings, it looks like a bargain. Revenue can grow in the mid-20s for a long time, and earnings growth should significantly outpace that level thanks to price increases protected by its wide moat.

news.Title: Is ASML Holding NV's Stock a Buy Ahead of Its Q3 Earnings Report Wednesday?
news.Content:
ASML (NASDAQ:ASML) doesn't get as much attention as chip stocks like Nvidia do, but the European semiconductor capital equipment specialist is arguably just as crucial to the AI boom.

ASML is the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment, which is used by manufacturers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing , Intel , and Samsung to make the world's most advanced chips.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The company is downstream from fabless chip companies like Nvidia in the AI boom, but it's set to reap the rewards of surging demand for AI chips, including the memory chip shortage and the supply expansion now underway.

With ASML set to report third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, let's review what to expect from the company to determine if the stock is a buy.

Image source: Image source: The Motley Fool.

Can ASML keep climbing?

ASML stock is up 64% this year, benefiting from the larger boom in chip stocks in the spring, though it's traded sideways over the last few months.

Investors bid the stock up on expectations that its growth will accelerate due to semiconductor supply shortages, and that seems to be happening.

The analyst consensus calls for ASML's revenue to jump 56% to 11.7 billion euros, or $13.1 billion, and for adjusted earnings per share to nearly double from 5.49 euros to 10.76 euros. ASML's quarterly results are lumpy as its machines are very expensive and it sells around 100 of them each quarter. However, it also earns significant revenue from installed base management, which covers maintenance, repair, and upgrades to existing machines.

The forecast calls for ASML's strongest revenue growth since 2023, and significantly higher than the 24% growth it reported in the second quarter. The boom in memory explains part of the growth surge as the company has projected more than 75% growth in memory systems for the year, due to ramping demand for high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, and top customers like TSMC and Intel are expanding production of more advanced nodes.

Is ASML a buy heading into earnings?

With the stock having roughly doubled over the last year, ASML can't be considered cheap anymore. It currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 57, which is higher than many of its chip-stock peers, such as Nvidia, as well as ETFs that track the industry, such as the Van Eck Semiconductor ETF .

Story Continues

However, ASML is a rare monopoly, as the only maker of EUV machines, that investors have access to, and its market power grows as demand for more advanced chips leads manufacturers to buy more EUV machines. The company also has a less advanced deep ultraviolet (DUV) machine, with which it competes with Chinese companies and others such as Nikon and Canon . While others are developing EUV technology, the company's lead in the industry seems reasonably secure due to its experience, specialized supply chain, technical expertise, and relationships.

Finally, investors will want to watch ASML's guidance in the report. The company has issued 2030 revenue guidance of 44 billion-60 billion euros, but analysts' expectations for the third quarter show it's already reached that rate, meaning it could soon raise its long-term guidance. The company has already raised its 2026 guidance to 43 billion-45 billion euros from an earlier forecast of 36 billion-40 billion euros.

Based on the momentum in the business, the monopoly in EUVs, and the growth in chip demand from AI, ASML looks like a strong buy ahead of its report. Though its quarterly results are difficult to predict, the company should achieve considerable growth over the next few years.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Intel aims to boost AI turnaround with new GPU chips to take on Nvidia
news.Content:
Intel's ( INTC ) turnaround effort is getting a strong boost from the global AI build-out, which is driving increased demand for its central processing units (CPUs) .

But the company is also expanding further into the graphics processing unit (GPU) market with the debut of its Intel GPU D-Series processors . Formerly codenamed Crescent Island, the D-Series chips are designed for AI inferencing, running AI models and services.

Rather than individual chips that slot into server blades like Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Blackwell processors, Intel's D-Series GPUs are deployed via PCIe cards, similar in appearance to the graphics cards gamers install in desktop computers.

Intel said it's working with a number of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, and others to roll out D-Series systems, including ASUS ( 2357.TW ), HPE ( HPE ), Dell ( DELL ), Supermicro, and others.

Intel has been working to gain a greater foothold in the GPU market, ranging from consumer products to the data center, including its Gaudi AI accelerator and GPU Flex Series cards.

Intel stock is up 183% year to date and roughly 175% over the past 12 months, largely driven by interest in its CPUs.

The processors, which fell out of favor in the early days of the generative AI explosion, have become increasingly important for AI providers and data center builders with the advent of AI agents.

That's because while GPUs and AI accelerators power the AI models and agents that rely on them, the tasks agents perform, such as sorting through databases, launching apps, loading websites, and more, run on CPUs.

But Intel is facing increasing competition in the CPU data center race from longtime rival AMD ( AMD ), which is rapidly growing its share of data center revenue in the space.

Arm-based ( ARM ) CPUs are also gaining a greater foothold in the data center, thanks to Nvidia's decision to launch standalone CPU racks running its Grace chip .

Qualcomm ( QCOM ) has also entered the fight with its own Arm-based CPUs , AI accelerators, memory products, and networking capabilities as it seeks to diversify beyond its reliance on the smartphone market.

news.Title: ASML vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
Demand for advanced computing power links two of the chip industry's best-known companies. ASML Holding (NASDAQ:ASML) makes the lithography systems that chipmakers use to print circuits on silicon, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), known as TSMC, is a contract manufacturer that makes chips for other companies.

The two also work together. In a joint release in September, ASML and TSMC said they had formed an initiative to move High NA EUV lithography to larger photomasks, and that TSMC intends to use ASML's High NA technology in high-volume manufacturing for advanced nodes starting in 2030.

Investors often compare them because their businesses are closely linked, even though their financial profiles differ.

The case for ASML

ASML supplies chipmakers with lithography systems and related software and services used to print circuit patterns on silicon wafers. Its flagship products include Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) and Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) machines used to produce advanced chips. ASML says it is currently the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems. According to ASML's 2025 annual report, four customers accounted for about 61% of ASML's 2025 net sales.

ASML reports its results in euros, and the annual figures here are approximate conversions to U.S. dollars. In 2025, revenue reached nearly $36.6 billion, up roughly 15.6% from the previous year. The company reported net income of about $10.8 billion for the period, resulting in a net margin of nearly 29.4%.

For the quarter ended June 28, 2026, ASML reported net sales of 9.3 billion euros and a gross margin of 54%. In July, it raised its 2026 outlook to total net sales of 43-45 billion euros.

Based on its December 2025 balance sheet, ASML's debt-to-equity ratio, calculated from total debt and shareholders' equity, is about 0.2x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholders' equity, indicating modest borrowing relative to shareholders' equity.

The current ratio, also calculated from the balance sheet, measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with assets expected to convert to cash within a year, and is roughly 1.3x. Free cash flow, which ASML calculates as operating cash flow minus purchases of property, plant, and equipment and intangible assets, was approximately $12.4 billion for the year.

The case for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

TSMC operates as a pure-play foundry, meaning it manufactures chips for customers rather than designing its own. In 2025, it manufactured 12,682 products for 534 customers, with demand coming from markets such as high-performance computing and smartphones. Advanced technologies at 7 nanometers and below accounted for 74% of its 2025 wafer revenue.

Story Continues

TSMC reports its results in New Taiwan dollars, and the annual figures here are approximate conversions to U.S. dollars.

In 2025, revenue reached roughly $121.3 billion, up about 31.6% in New Taiwan dollars and 35.9% in U.S. dollars, according to TSMC. The company earned net income of about $54.7 billion, for a net margin of approximately 45.1%.

For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, TSMC reported revenue up 36% year over year in New Taiwan dollars, with a gross margin of 67.7%.

Based on TSMC's December 2025 balance sheet, I calculate a current ratio of roughly 2.5x to 2.6x, depending on which of TSMC's year-end statements is used. That means current assets are about two and a half times current liabilities.

The debt-to-equity ratio, calculated as interest-bearing debt divided by total equity, is approximately 0.2x, a modest level of debt relative to shareholder equity. Free cash flow, calculated by subtracting capital expenditures from operating cash flow, reached about NT$1.0 trillion, or approximately $32 billion at the converted rate, for the fiscal year.

Risk profile comparison

ASML's customer concentration is a risk, since a change in spending plans at any one of its four largest customers can move its results. Because its customers are chipmakers that decide when to add capacity, a slowdown in industry spending would reduce demand for its systems.

Export controls are another factor. ASML's annual report says, "Changes in export controls may have a material impact on our business for example on the sales volume, mix and timing," and China accounted for about 29% of its 2025 net sales in the geographic breakdown of its annual report.

According to its interim report, which attributes sales to the location of customers' facilities, China's share fell to about 16% of net sales in the first half of 2026.

TSMC's business requires heavy, continuing investment in factories and technology, with capital expenditures of about $40.9 billion in 2025, according to TSMC. Geopolitical risk is the other main concern, since the majority of its principal production facilities are in Taiwan. TSMC also faces competition from other foundries, including Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), which TSMC's chief executive described as a formidable competitor on the April 2026 earnings call, and Samsung Electronics (OTC:SSNLF), which TrendForce estimates ranked second in foundry revenue in the second quarter of 2026.

TSMC's customer base is also concentrated at the top, as its annual report shows two customers accounted for 19% and 17% of 2025 net revenue. Demand for TSMC's chips also depends on its customers' end markets, including smartphones and consumer electronics, so weakness in those categories would affect sales.

Valuation comparison

TSMC has the lower forward P/E of the two in the table, and the two companies are close on price-to-sales. The P/S ratio measures a company's market value against its past twelve months of sales. The forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

While TSMC looks like the better buy to me, I'd be a patient buyer, as shares of both companies have risen sharply over the past year and TSMC's production is concentrated in Taiwan.

My reasoning starts with the fact that each business depends on its customers. Both are concentrated.

TSMC's two largest customers accounted for about 36% of its 2025 net revenue, according to its annual report, and four customers accounted for about 61% of ASML's 2025 net sales. TSMC also serves 534 customers in total, so the business has a broader base beyond its largest accounts. ASML says it is currently the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems, which is a strong foundation, though it also means a handful of chipmakers shape demand.

TSMC also carries the lower forward earnings multiple in the table, which adds to its appeal for me.

If I were buying, I'd start with a modest TSMC position and add to it over time, planning to hold for years. Sharp pullbacks can happen with both stocks, and if the business still looked sound after one, I'd treat it as a chance to add more.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Elon Musk says Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) and SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX ) could eventually become unusually strong chip manufacturers by applying one of their existing strengths: designing highly customized production equipment . Speaking via livestream at the X Takeover event outside Tesla's Gigafactory in Austin, Musk acknowledged that he currently has no idea how to make microchips, but added, we'll figure it out. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA. Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. His argument is that the manufacturing process itself could become a competitive advantage. Musk said that after touring rival facilities, he had not seen much customized equipment, while Tesla and SpaceX have extensive experience building specialized machinery for their own factories and products. In his view, that capability could allow his companies to improve chip-manufacturing processes rather than simply rely on standard industry equipment. The comments fit with Musk's increasingly aggressive semiconductor ambitions. Earlier this month, Musk said Tesla and SpaceX intend to build and operate the planned Terafab AI chip complex themselves , while leaving open the possibility that TSMC ( NYSE:TSM ) could sublease part of the facility. Responding to speculation that TSMC would ultimately own and run the fab, Musk wrote: No, we will build and run the fab. Let there be ZERO doubt about that. That would represent a major strategic shift for Musk's companies. Tesla and SpaceX already depend heavily on advanced semiconductors for autonomous-driving systems, AI training, robotics, communications and other compute-intensive applications. Bringing more chip production in-house could give Musk greater control over cost, supply and product design. Investor Takeaway I think the key point here is that Musk does not appear to be treating chip manufacturing as a conventional outsourcing exercise. He is talking about redesigning the manufacturing process itself . That matters because Tesla and SpaceX have historically tried to vertically integrate technologies they view as strategically important, from batteries and vehicles to rockets and satellite networks. If that same approach extends to semiconductors, Terafab could eventually become much more than a capacity project. It could become an attempt to build a proprietary manufacturing system optimized around Musk's AI workloads. But the execution risk is enormous. Leading-edge chip fabrication requires extraordinary precision, engineering expertise and capital, areas where established foundries such as TSMC have spent decades building advantages. The opportunity is potentially huge, but so is the technological gap Musk's companies would need to close. news.Title: Not Sandisk, Not Intel. This Stock Will Lead the S&P 500 Next Year
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) has had a great year so far. The average annual return of the S&P 500 is about 10%, and with it sitting at about 14.5% right now, it has been a good year. There are still a few months left, so the chances of it ending up even higher are quite good.

While the S&P 500 as a whole is doing well, a few individual performers stand out. Sandisk holds the title for best-performing S&P 500 stock this year, rising about 590% in 2026. Intel is another top performer, increasing nearly 200% so far this year. There are a handful of companies that also have had strong runs, including AMD .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

So, which stock will lead the S&P 500 higher next year? I think it will be a familiar face, and it won't be one of these three.

Some stocks have gotten ahead of themselves

With the returns some stocks are delivering this year, it's pretty easy to guess that next year may not be as kind to these stocks. Many companies have far outgrown their business results and are trading at inflated valuations, such as Intel and AMD. These two trade for 70 and 81 times forward earnings, respectively. This showcases just how expensive they are. Others, like Sandisk, operate in a cyclical market, and the stock market is wary of giving it a standard valuation due to fears of the memory chip industry seeing a cyclical downturn.

Regardless, there are a handful of stocks that were abandoned to pave the way for these to rise, and the most obvious one is Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Nvidia led the S&P 500 in performance during 2023 and 2024, and I think it has a strong shot at leading it again in 2027. Why? Its stock has been ignored compared to some of its peers.

Nvidia is dirt cheap compared to its peers

It's hard to say that the largest company in the world by market cap isn't getting a fair shake, but that's exactly what's happening. As mentioned above, AMD trades at over 80 times forward earnings. Nvidia trades at 25.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

These two companies operate in the same industry (namely, graphics processing units , or GPUs), and Nvidia is growing its data center business (the segment most exposed to artificial intelligence (AI)) at a faster pace. In Q2, Nvidia's data center division grew at a 117% pace to $89 billion. AMD's data center division grew at a 107% pace to $6.7 billion. Nvidia is still winning, and there's no reason to give AMD a ridiculous premium as a result.

Story Continues

Another factor is that the market hasn't priced in practically any of 2027's growth into Nvidia's stock price. The S&P 500 trades for about 20 times forward earnings. The slight premium Nvidia now commands is worth it given its positioning in the AI boom and strong track record of performance. However, Nvidia is also expected to grow its revenue by 70% next year. But Nvidia's current 25 times forward earnings valuation implies that its stock will grow at a market-average pace next year (about 10%).

That's a major mismatch, and I think it suggests Nvidia is poised for an exceptional year and could lead the S&P 500 in performance. While there could be others that sneak up on investors and outperform Nvidia, Nvidia is one of the few companies that has given investors high visibility into its future growth. Management has undergirded nearly every step along the way, so this 70% growth could also be a major undershoot.

With Nvidia expected to grow revenue by 70% or more next year, I think it's a no-brainer buy right now.

news.Title: Analog Devices (ADI) vs. TXN and ON: Can AI Infrastructure and Acquisitions Drive Its Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Is ADI a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Analog Devices, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $378.78, and ADI gained more than 7% since then. The gain appears to reflect improving earnings expectations, supported by recovering industrial demand and expanding AI data center activity across power and optical applications. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ADI. Analog Devices, Inc.'s share was trading at $405.93 as of October 8th 2026. ADI's trailing and forward P/E were 45.75 and 23.20 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor company pitched as a great investment. ADI shares gained 80.16% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Texas Instruments Incorporated and Microchip Technology Incorporated gained 67.85% and 25.01%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

Portogas D Ace/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about 12 High Growth Semiconductor Stocks to Buy Now and ADI ranked #5 in that article. ADI returned 2.20% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ADI. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADI. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADI) designs and makes analog, mixed-signal, power management, radio-frequency, and digital signal-processing chips used in industries like manufacturing, automobiles, communications, healthcare, and aerospace. Its investment case increasingly rests on two forces working together: a recovery in traditional industrial and automotive chip demand, and rising demand for its chips in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

AI data centers need increasingly complex power delivery, cooling, and signal-processing systems, giving Analog Devices, Inc. a second growth engine beyond its traditional markets. Revenue over the past year came in at $13.9 billion, up a strong 33.7%, with healthy profit margins across the board. The stock trades at a premium to its peer group, meaning investors are betting not just on the current recovery, but on the company sustaining above-average growth and profitability going forward.

Story Continues

The bullish case centers on Analog Devices, Inc. expanding its footprint in industrial and automotive markets while becoming more essential to AI infrastructure (see whether Cadence and Analog Devices could capture more of the smart-vehicle opportunity ) . As AI computing needs grow, servers require more advanced power and signal-processing components, which benefits the company both from overall AI spending and from selling more chips per system. Its July 2026 acquisition of Empower Semiconductor supports this, aimed at strengthening its power-delivery capabilities for high-density AI systems.

Management followed this in September with an agreement to acquire Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion in cash, plus up to $200 million more tied to performance targets, adding power-efficient AI chips for edge devices. (see the opportunities and risks behind ADI's $1.35 billion bet on edge-AI chips )

If AI spending stays strong while industrial and auto demand keeps normalizing, bulls believe this could mean several years of growth rather than a short-term rebound. The company also generated $4.3 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year, giving it $2.3 billion in cash and enough financial flexibility to keep funding acquisitions and investments despite carrying $9.1 billion in total debt.

Wall Street analysts broadly share this optimism. The consensus 12-month price target sits at $470.25, suggesting nearly 29% upside from the current price of $365.07, with individual targets ranging from $365 to $675. Reaching that target would require earnings to grow substantially faster than what analysts currently forecast, meaning the stock's upside case depends heavily on continued strong earnings growth rather than just steady performance.

That said, weaker industrial demand, slower AI spending, or geopolitical disruptions remain key risks. So far, the numbers support the bullish case: gross margin recently climbed to 67.3%, up meaningfully from 62.2% a year earlier, while quarterly cash generated from operations jumped 38% year over year. This suggests the recovery is translating into real profitability, not just higher sales volume. One risk worth watching is that Greater China has historically made up 15% to 20% of revenue, which exposes the company to U.S. export restrictions and competition from China's domestic chipmakers. Combined with its reliance on Taiwan-based manufacturing, this leaves limited room for missteps given how richly the stock is already valued.

Another risk for the stock is failing to win a place in next-generation AI systems. Buying advanced power-delivery technology does not guarantee that customers will choose ADI's chips. Driven by demand for more efficient servers, manufacturers must select components that meet strict performance and reliability requirements. ADI's expanded portfolio still needs to secure those customer approvals. Chip suppliers depend on winning a place in system designs before production begins. Losing those opportunities could limit chip sales per server even while AI investment grows. In our opinion, this risk could pressure ADI's price multiples if its AI capabilities fail to translate into meaningful customer wins.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 102 hedge fund portfolios held Analog Devices, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 109 in the previous quarter. This modest pullback suggests institutional investors remain broadly comfortable with the company's margins, recovery, and AI exposure, even as some grow more cautious on valuation. By comparison, Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ:TXN) was held by 111 hedge funds, up sharply from 71, while Microchip Technology Incorporated (NASDAQ:MCHP) was held by 81 hedge funds, up from 69, and ON Semiconductor Corporation (NASDAQ:ON) was held by 86 hedge funds, up from 58. This divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Texas Instruments Incorporated during the quarter, while Microchip Technology Incorporated and ON Semiconductor Corporation also saw meaningful increases in interest, even as enthusiasm for Analog Devices, Inc. cooled slightly despite its strong fundamentals.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for the Analog Devices, Inc., with just 1.99% of its float sold short, below Texas Instruments Incorporated at 2.41% and well below Microchip Technology Incorporated at 8.03%. Bearish positioning is also far lower than ON Semiconductor Corporation where short interest stands at 10.43% of float. This suggests that Analog Devices, Inc.'s valuation and geopolitical risks are drawing relatively little outright bearish conviction compared with its peers.

Valuation Analysis

ADI's forward P/E is 23.20x. Texas Instruments Incorporated, Microchip Technology Incorporated, and ON Semiconductor Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 27.55x, 20.53x, and 16.50x, respectively. ADI's own forward P/E was 24.94x on October 31, 2025, putting its current multiple approximately 7% below that level. We believe ADI's premium to Microchip and ON Semiconductor reflects expectations for stronger earnings growth from recovering industrial demand and AI infrastructure spending. However, a lower multiple than last year does not establish that the stock is cheap. Analog Devices, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share rose from $6.38 in fiscal 2024 to $7.79 in fiscal 2025, an increase of approximately 22%, but remained below the $9.57 earned in fiscal 2022. This shows that earnings recovered in fiscal 2025 after earlier declines, rather than growing consistently over the three-year period. We believe 23.20 times expected earnings could be reasonable if that recovery develops into sustained growth, but the 22% increase alone does not justify its premium. If AI demand helps ADI grow earnings beyond its previous peak, the current valuation could offer a reasonable entry point for long-term investors.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN) by The Wolf of Harcourt Street in January 2025, which highlighted analog stabilization, shareholder returns, and manufacturing capacity investments. TXN's stock price has appreciated by approximately 58.57% since our coverage. We believe ADI could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if earnings growth continues beyond the cyclical recovery

Analog Devices, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While ADI offers attractive long-term potential if recovering industrial and automotive demand and expanding AI power-delivery capabilities sustain earnings growth beyond the cyclical rebound, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. news.Title: Rivian Automotive (RIVN) vs. TSLA and F: Can Improving Margins and Its R2 Midsize SUV Unlock Profitable Growth?
news.Content:
Is RIVN a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Rivian Automotive, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on RIVN. Rivian Automotive, Inc.'s share was trading at $13.96 as of October 9th 2026.

This isn't the first time we see an automaker pitched as a great investment. Unfortunately, RIVN shares lost 29.17% of their value year to date. Comparable stocks like Ford Motor Company (F) lost 7.24% of their value during the same period. Why are auto stocks declining so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

In April, we published an article about the 10 Best Car Stocks to Buy in 2026 and RIVN ranked #4 in that article. Unfortunately, RIVN has lost 6.55% since then, likely reflecting concerns about cash burn, share dilution, and weaker EV demand. This article explains why TD Cowen, an investment banking firm within TD Securities, also turned bullish on RIVN ahead of the R2 launch. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Rivian Automotive, Inc. (NASDAQ:RIVN) designs and builds electric vehicles, including the R1T pickup, R1S SUV, commercial vans, and its newly launched R2 midsize SUV, along with the software, charging, fleet management, and autonomous-driving technology that support them. Its central investment case right now is the R2 platform, and that's key to understanding whether Rivian can turn years of heavy manufacturing investment into a scalable, higher-volume EV business.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The roughly $45,000 R2 began customer deliveries in June 2026 and was built for lower costs, simpler assembly, and higher production volumes. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue grew about 27% year over year to $1.7 billion, and Rivian posted a record $179 million in quarterly gross profit, marking four straight quarters of positive gross margin. That's real progress, but the company still lost $2.58 per share on a trailing basis, and its stock trades at close to 3.7 times trailing sales — a sign that investors are paying less for what Rivian earns today and more for what they expect the R2 ramp to deliver in profits and cash flow down the road.

The bullish case for Rivian Automotive rests on the idea that higher R2 production volumes and its lower-cost design can steadily improve the company's unit economics. Rivian absorbed about $100 million in one-time costs tied to ramping up R2 production, while its software and services business brought in $515 million of second-quarter revenue at a strong 42% gross margin, generating $215 million in profit that helped offset a $36 million loss on the automotive side. Management is aiming for positive per-unit gross margins on the R2 by the end of 2026, so how quickly the platform can scale while cutting manufacturing costs is central to the turnaround story.

Story Continues

Management also raised its full-year delivery outlook by 3,000 vehicles to a range of 65,000 to 70,000 units, narrowed its expected adjusted EBITDA loss to $1.80-$2.00 billion, and trimmed planned capital spending to $1.70-$1.80 billion. A technology partnership with Volkswagen, potentially worth up to $5.8 billion, is focused on next-generation vehicle electronics and software, with another $1 billion in financing expected later in 2026. After a July equity raise, Rivian had $7.16 billion in available cash and liquidity, enough for roughly two years of runway at its current spending pace. If R2 volumes grow and manufacturing gets more efficient, bulls believe this liquidity and Volkswagen's backing give Rivian enough room to move toward sustainable profitability before funding becomes a pressing concern. You can check out whether Tesla or Rivian makes the better EV stock investment here .

Wall Street also leans bullish: the average analyst price target of $19.23 implies roughly 21% upside from Rivian's recent $15.95 share price, while the median target of $18.50 points to about 16% upside. The highest target of $25 suggests as much as 57% upside, while the lowest, at $13, implies around 19% downside. A more conservative, probability-weighted fair-value estimate of $17.21 implies about 8% upside, reflecting caution about how sustainable Rivian's recent margin gains really are. With trailing free cash flow around negative $3.5 billion, investors should watch closely whether rising revenue and margins eventually translate into real earnings and cash flow strong enough to support these price targets.

The biggest risk to this story is the quality of Rivian's recent gross-profit improvement. If the manufacturing turnaround were as strong as it looks, margins should hold up even without help from regulatory credits — but they don't. Regulatory credits added $164 million to gross profit in the first half of the year, accounting for roughly 55% of that profit; excluding those credits, gross margin was only about 4.7%. Those credits are expected to largely disappear in the second half, meaning the underlying improvement is smaller than the headline numbers suggest. Rivian is also still burning significant cash, and part of its liquidity cushion came from a roughly $1.5 billion equity offering in July that added 75 million new shares. Combined with exposure to Chinese battery materials, tariffs, critical-mineral restrictions, high financing costs, shifting EV incentives, and the risk of further dilution, the company has little room for delays in the R2 rollout.

Another risk for the stock is pricing pressure in the EV market. Rivian may need discounts to win R2 buyers, weakening the benefit of its lower-cost design. Driven by competition, larger automakers can use price cuts and incentives to defend sales. Rivian warns that better-funded rivals can absorb these cuts more easily than it can. sec.gov Its turnaround depends on keeping enough of each vehicle's selling price to cover production costs. Higher deliveries could therefore fail to improve profitability if discounts offset manufacturing savings. In our opinion, this could pressure Rivian's price multiples if R2 sales grow without delivering the expected improvement in profits.

Hedge fund positioning shows a cautious signal. As per our database, 40 hedge fund portfolios held Rivian Automotive at the end of the second quarter, down from 45 in the previous quarter. That decline points to institutional investors turning somewhat more cautious on Rivian's R2 launch and turnaround story despite its improving numbers. By comparison, Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) was held by 116 hedge funds, down from 123, while Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID) was held by 23 hedge funds, unchanged from the prior quarter, and Ford Motor Company (NYSE:F) was held by 50, also unchanged. Rivian Automotive saw the steepest drop in hedge fund interest among the four, suggesting institutional conviction is softening even as the company's operating outlook improves.

Short interest data also paints a fairly concerning picture for Rivian Automotive, with 14.90% of its shares sold short — far above Tesla at 2.01% and Ford Motor Company at 3.85%, though still well below Lucid Group at 57.19%. This suggests Rivian's negative cash flow, dilution risk, and dependence on a successful R2 launch are drawing noticeably more skepticism than Tesla or Ford face, even if bearish bets remain far less extreme than those against Lucid.

Valuation Analysis

RIVN's EV/revenue is 3.73x. Tesla, Inc., Lucid Group, Inc., and Ford Motor Company trade at EV/revenue multiples of 14.22x, 2.93x, and 0.98x, respectively. RIVN's own EV/revenue was 4.08x on December 31, 2025, putting its current valuation approximately 9% below that level. We believe the current valuation reflects expectations that the R2 rollout will increase sales and lower manufacturing costs. However, Rivian's premium to Lucid and Ford requires evidence that growing sales can produce sustainable profits, while its discount to Tesla alone does not establish that it is cheap. Rivian Automotive, Inc.'s second-quarter revenue increased approximately 27% year over year to $1.66 billion, but its automotive business still recorded a $36 million gross loss. We believe 3.73 times revenue can be justified if higher R2 volumes spread factory costs across more vehicles and improve margins enough to substantially reduce cash burn. If Rivian can achieve those improvements before needing substantial additional funding, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point for investors willing to accept the risks of its turnaround.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Rivian Automotive, Inc. (RIVN) by LegitosaurusRex in November 2024, which highlighted the R2 and R3 lineup, Volkswagen funding, cost cuts, and domestic manufacturing advantage. RIVN's stock price has appreciated by approximately 42.28% since our coverage. We believe RIVN could be a good long-term investment, provided higher R2 production improves profitability and reduces cash burn before substantial additional funding is needed.

news.Title: Elon Musk Sets the Record Straight on Terafab. What It Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks.
news.Content:
Elon Musk's ambitious Terafab semiconductor project has put Intel (INTC), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM), and SpaceX (SPCX) in the spotlight. A report about a potential partnership between TSMC and Terafab raised questions about Intel's role in the project. However, Musk's subsequent comments cast the initial speculation in a different light.

At the heart of the uncertainty is how the three companies could fit into Musk's plans to build an advanced semiconductor manufacturing operation in Texas. While Intel has already emerged as a key technology partner, the prospect of TSMC's involvement raised concerns that the U.S. chipmaker could be sidelined. Musk later sought to address those concerns, challenging some of the assumptions surrounding the reported discussions.

More News from Barchart

'When You Say I Should Pay $100 Billion, Then I'm Starting To Do A Little Math': Bill Gates Said He'd Happily Pay 'Over $10 Billion In Taxes' But Some Are Asking Too Much

Dan Ives Calls SpaceX's $40B Nvidia Chip Debt Plan a 'Smart Move'

Dear Johnson & Johnson Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

So, what is really happening with Terafab, and what do Musk's comments mean for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX stocks? More importantly, what is the biggest takeaway for investors? Let's take a closer look.

Intel, TSMC, and Terafab: Musk Sets the Record Straight

Culpium, a Substack covering the Asian technology world, reported on Oct. 2, citing sources, that TSMC was exploring ways to help Terafab operate its semiconductor factories in Texas. "Just discussions, but something may come of it," Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA), wrote in a post on X in response to the report.

Intel shares slid 5.7% over last Monday and Tuesday as investors interpreted the news as a sign of increased competition for the chipmaker. Still, Musk acknowledged in response to a separate post on X that any chips supplied by TSMC would likely supplement those provided by Intel. Intel became Terafab's first named semiconductor manufacturing partner in April, and Musk subsequently said the project planned to use Intel's next-generation 14A manufacturing process.

Concerns about Intel's role eased last Wednesday after Musk and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan sought to clarify the chipmaker's involvement in Terafab. Tan told Bloomberg that Intel would remain involved in the project. Meanwhile, Tesla commentator Herbert Ong wrote on X last Tuesday that "The likeliest deal has TSMC owning and running the fab," before later clarifying that he meant "a PIECE of the fab." Musk swiftly rejected that suggestion, responding to Ong's post: "No, we will build and run the fab. Let there be ZERO doubt about that." He also clarified that the discussions concerned only the possibility of TSMC leasing part of the planned site, without taking on an operational role.

Story Continues

Musk's Terafab Clarification Eases Intel Concerns but Leaves Room for TSMC Orders

Musk's clarification significantly changed the interpretation of the Terafab story. Rather than TSMC stepping in to operate part of the facility, its potential involvement would be limited to leasing a portion of the planned site.

Technically, such an arrangement could result in two separate semiconductor operations on the same broader campus. Terafab would remain under Musk's control, with Intel providing critical manufacturing technology. At the same time, TSMC could establish its own operations on the leased portion of the site.

Importantly, the sublease alone would not mean Terafab would use TSMC's process technology, TSMC would manufacture chips for the project, or TSMC would manage Terafab's production lines. TSMC is reportedly considering a multibillion-dollar manufacturing expansion in Texas, so the site could simply provide another location option. Still, Musk's earlier suggestion that TSMC's chips could supplement Intel's appears to leave open the possibility that TSMC could secure chip orders from Terafab.

What Musk's Terafab Clarification Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks

At this point, let's take a closer look at what Musk's clarification means for INTC, TSM, and SPCX stocks.

For Intel, Musk's clarification is the most reassuring development and, consequently, a positive for its stock. INTC shares closed slightly higher last Wednesday following the clarification, bucking a broader chip-sector selloff driven by rising bond yields. Musk's comments eased concerns that TSMC could diminish Intel's role in Terafab, preserving the chipmaker's opportunity to demonstrate the commercial viability of its 14A process technology, a key to its foundry turnaround.

For TSMC, the new interpretation is much less exciting than the original story. Under Musk's clarification, TSMC's potential role would be closer to that of a tenant or neighboring manufacturer. Such an arrangement could still offer strategic benefits if TSMC is looking to expand its capacity in Texas, but the bigger question is whether it would secure any chip orders from Terafab. After all, dual-sourcing is common practice in the semiconductor industry. For now, however, the implications for TSM stock remain largely neutral.

For SpaceX, the implications are more mixed. On the positive side, retaining operational control would allow SpaceX and Tesla to coordinate chip designs, production schedules, and manufacturing capacity around their own needs. That fits SpaceX's broader goal of securing chip supplies to support both companies' AI initiatives. The downside, however, is execution risk, given the immense complexity of operating a leading-edge semiconductor fab. TSMC has spent decades refining its manufacturing expertise, improving production yields, and mastering complex fabrication processes. Even with Intel providing its 14A technology, SpaceX would still need to overcome challenges involving equipment installation, engineering expertise, production yields, reliability, staffing, and supply chain management to manufacture advanced chips efficiently at a commercial scale.

The Biggest Takeaway

The biggest takeaway is that this is no longer primarily an Intel-versus-TSMC story. Musk's clarification suggests TSMC would not be challenging Intel's role as Terafab's manufacturing technology partner. The more important question is whether SpaceX and Tesla can successfully operate Terafab themselves, with Intel providing the manufacturing technology and TSMC potentially operating nearby rather than taking over the project.

news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor Stock Hits a New All-Time: Is it Too Late to Invest?
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM) is a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) market. It dominates the foundry market, with a market share of around 70%. It's the go-to foundry for many top tech companies, and thus, if demand for AI chips is growing, that's great news for Taiwan Semi.

This year, the tech stock is up around 50%, recently hitting a new all-time high due to the hype and excitement around its business. At around $2.3 trillion in market cap, however, it's also among the most highly valued stocks on U.S. markets. The big question investors may have is whether the stock has gotten too expensive. Is it too late to invest in Taiwan Semi?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Taiwan Semi is expected to release its full quarterly results for its most recent period on Thursday. The numbers are likely to be strong, with analysts expecting that for a sixth consecutive quarter, Taiwan Semi will post record earnings, thanks to AI-driven demand. The expectation is that profits will be up by 65%, totaling $23.4 billion.

The tech company recently announced that its revenue thus far in 2026 has risen by more than 40%. Meanwhile, with tech spending remaining feverish as companies try to stay ahead of their rivals in AI development, the outlook is likely to remain fairly strong for Taiwan Semi in the foreseeable future, as demand doesn't appear to be slowing anytime soon.

Although Taiwan Semi's business is booming, its valuation arguably isn't all that high. The tech stock is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 21 (based on analyst expectations). Thus, it may still command significant market share in the years to come, enabling it to continue to benefit from the ongoing investments related to AI.

Taiwan Semi's stock has pulled back from its recent highs, but with a bright future ahead and a dominant market position, it's hard not to like the stock as a long-term investment. Despite its gains this year, Taiwan Semi may still be a good buy right now.

news.Title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Has Millions in This 1 Monopoly Chip Stock
news.Content:
Following billionaire hedge fund managers is a great way to source investing ideas. While you shouldn't blindly follow them in every trade, looking at what they own and have recently bought is a smart investment strategy.

One billionaire I follow is Stanley Druckenmiller, who manages the Duquesne Family Office. Druckenmiller's portfolio is full of companies from all industries, so he's not focused on tech specifically. However, his second-largest holding is a notable name in the tech space: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Druckenmiller's portfolio has a sizable stake in TSMC, and I think it's a smart buy for many investors.

A hefty chunk of his portfolio is invested in TSMC

Investors get a peek at any fund with a portfolio larger than $100 million 45 days after each quarter ends. So, the information available now shows his holdings as of June 30. This information was made available on July 15, so it's a bit stale by now. However, the key is to find managers that hold onto stocks for a long time, since being directly on time to follow their moves isn't as critical.

At the end of the second quarter, Druckenmiller owned about 590,000 shares of TSMC, valued at over $280 million. That makes up about 6.5% of the firm's invested assets, good enough for his second-largest holding. That suggests a lot of bullish sentiment toward TSMC's stock, so why is he so sure TSMC will be a winner?

Taiwan Semiconductor is nearly a monopoly

While several other chip foundries compete with Taiwan Semiconductor, none can match its scale. In Q2, TSMC was estimated to account for 72.5% of global chip foundry revenue.

If you're a company that's going to have a chip fabricated by an outside manufacturer, it's very likely that TSMC is on top of the list to go to. It has the scale to produce the chips and leading technology as well. That one-two punch makes TSMC a top partner in the chip world, and it shows up in its results.

During Q2, its revenue rose 33% year over year while earnings per share increased over 70%.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

This coming quarter is expected to be even better, with revenue growth estimated to be about 47%, according to Wall Street analysts. That will be a fairly sizable growth acceleration, ranking it among the best quarters Taiwan Semiconductor has seen in recent history.

Story Continues

This confirms why Druckenmiller has invested in TSMC, but is it still a good buy now? After all, the latest information we have on his holdings was from June 30.

I think the best way to value Taiwan Semiconductor's stock is to value it using its forward earnings ratio and next year's projected earnings. From this perspective, TSMC tends to reach about 30 times forward earnings at the end of the year, so there is a bit of upside left. However, when you use next year's earnings projection to value the stock, there is even more upside remaining, mainly due to the artificial intelligence (AI) arms race being far from over.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

This makes Taiwan Semiconductor a great multi-year play, and with Wall Street expecting 35% revenue growth next year, it's clear that Taiwan Semiconductor still has a lot of room to run over the next few years.

I think that makes Taiwan Semiconductor an excellent investment as it has billionaire backing, partnerships with some of the biggest AI companies in the world, and trades at a reasonable price tag. Furthermore, its size is so massive that it practically has a monopoly in the chip fabrication space. All that adds up to make TSMC one of the top stocks to buy right now .

news.Title: 5 Dividend Growth Stocks to Buy Ahead of US Inflation Data Release
news.Content:
All three major U.S. stock indices ended the previous week in the green zone as equities made a rebound from a tech-led sell-off observed earlier in the week. Meanwhile, assurances from U.S. President Donald Trump that America would not attack Iran before the midterm elections might have helped ease some immediate supply panic and kept the stock market buoyant.

However, as third-quarter earnings season kicks off this week, particularly for banks, uncertainties remain in the form of soon-to-be released inflation data, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's ‌next policy decision.

Against this backdrop, stock market participants might remain worried about investing in high-multiple, pure-growth stocks.

Instead, dividend growth stocks offer an appealing sweet spot: combining steady income generation, lower equity volatility and long-term compounding power amid macro uncertainty.

These companies boast a proven track record of increasing payouts, underscoring the balance-sheet strength and cash-flow resilience required to navigate a market environment where traditional growth narratives are being reassessed.

Stocks with a strong history of year-over-year dividend growth can help build a resilient portfolio with greater potential for capital appreciation compared to simple dividend-paying or high-yield stocks.

We have selected five dividend growth stocks, Enersys Inc. ENS, Micron Technology MU, Cheesecake Factory CAKE, Suncor Energy SU, and Taiwan Semiconductor TSM, which could be solid choices for your portfolio.

Why Is Dividend Growth Better?

Stocks with a strong history of dividend growth are typically associated with mature companies that are less prone to sharp market swings, allowing them to serve as a hedge against economic or political uncertainty as well as broader market volatility. Their steadily rising payouts provide some measure of downside protection.

These companies are generally backed by solid fundamentals, making them attractive long-term dividend-growth investments. Key strengths include durable business models, consistent profitability, expanding cash flows, healthy liquidity, strong balance sheets and attractive valuations.

A consistent history of dividend growth underscores the potential for continued growth ahead.

Although these stocks do not necessarily have the highest yields, they have outperformed the broader stock market and other dividend-paying stocks over an extended period.

As a result, selecting dividend-growth stocks appears to be a winning strategy when other key parameters are taken into account.

news.Title: Can NVTS' Alliance With Microchip Accelerate Its AI Power Growth?
news.Content:
Navitas Semiconductor NVTS is expanding its AI data center opportunity through its collaboration with Microchip Technology. The companies have developed an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for next-generation AI data center racks. The solution combines Microchip's digital power control and security technologies with NVTS' GaN power devices and is aligned with the Open Compute Project's 800V DC standard. The reference design includes hardware, software and design documentation to help data center developers reduce design time and bring new power systems to market faster.

The reference design uses NVTS' 650V GaNFast FETs and Microchip's dsPIC33AK digital signal controllers and TA100 CryptoAuthentication device. The system is designed to deliver up to 96% peak efficiency at full load, with a power density of 2,100 watts per cubic inch. It directly converts 800V DC to 6V DC by combining the 800V-to-50V and 50V-to-6V stages into a single converter. This approach is aimed at improving power conversion efficiency while supporting compact rack power systems.

The collaboration comes as AI data centers require higher power density and more efficient power delivery. Navitas has been focusing on this market as part of its broader shift toward high-power applications. In the second quarter of 2026, NVTS' high-power markets grew more than 50% year over year, while AI infrastructure is expected to account for more than one-third of total sales by the end of 2026. The company is also working on multiple AI data center programs tied to the transition toward 800V architectures.

The Microchip collaboration could help NVTS strengthen its position as more data center operators adopt 800V power systems. By combining NVTS' GaN technology with Microchip's digital control and security capabilities, the companies are offering customers a more complete solution for AI rack power. As 800V adoption expands, the new reference design could help NVTS gain additional design opportunities in the growing AI data center market.

How Competitors Fare Against NVTS

The company faces strong competition from ON Semiconductor ON and STMicroelectronics STM in the race to supply high-voltage solutions for AI data centers.

ON is expanding its presence in AI data center power as the industry moves toward 800V DC architectures. The company expects AI data center revenues to more than double in 2026, while silicon carbide revenues from AI data center applications are expected to grow nearly 60% year over year. The company expects its high-voltage revenues to accelerate as data centers adopt 800V DC distribution, increasing demand for its power solutions across the AI power tree.

Story Continues

STMicroelectronics is another semiconductor company gaining from rising AI data center power demand. The company reported 50% year-over-year growth in communication equipment and computer peripherals in the second quarter, supported by its AI-related customer programs. STM is already supplying microcontrollers, high-voltage power and analog products for the power stage of cloud AI systems and is building a pipeline for low-voltage power solutions. The company expects data center revenues to exceed $1 billion in 2026 and $2 billion in 2027 if current trends continue.

NVTS' Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of Navitas Semiconductor have rallied 51% year to date compared with the Zacks Electronics – Semiconductors industry's growth of 31%.

news.Title: Semtech Rises 154% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC shares have surged 154.1% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's growth of 45.2%. The stock also outperformed its industry peers, including Microchip Technology MCHP, ON Semiconductor ON and NXP Semiconductors NXPI. YTD, shares of Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors have gained 18.6%, 43.1% and 4.8%, respectively.

The outperformance of SMTC's shares raises the question: Does it still have room to run, or is it time for investors to consider taking profits? Let's find out.

YTD Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Semtech's 1.6T Ramp to Drive Data Center Growth

Semtech is seeing strong demand for its data center products as hyperscalers increase spending on AI infrastructure. The company's data center revenues reached a record $100 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 39% sequentially and 91% year over year. Growth was driven by continued strength in 800G products, along with the ramp of 1.6T CopperEdge and FiberEdge solutions. Management expects this momentum to continue, with data center revenues projected to increase 45% sequentially and 160% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

The 1.6T transition could become an important growth driver for Semtech. Management expects 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge products to account for more than 50% of total data center revenues in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Semtech is also gaining market share in optical connectivity, where its FiberEdge business has grown from about 18% market share in 800G two years ago to more than 50%. Further, the company expects its 1.6T FiberEdge market share to exceed 50% by the end of fiscal 2027.

The company is also preparing for the next stage of data center growth. Semtech is expanding its photonics portfolio through gain chips, high-power CW lasers, semiconductor optical amplifiers and photodiodes. These products are aimed at higher-speed applications, including 3.2T transceivers and co-packaged optics. Management expects its content per transceiver to increase from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars as data center speeds move from 800G to 3.2T.

Strong customer demand supports SMTC's prospects as well, with the company reporting that its backlog for the remainder of fiscal 2027 was fully booked and more than 70% of its target for fiscal 2028 was already covered. Management is also working with manufacturing partners to secure additional capacity for fiscal 2028 and beyond. If it can meet customer requirements and maintain its product momentum, the 1.6T ramp could remain an important driver of Semtech's data center growth over the next several quarters.

Story Continues

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 41.5% and 28.5%, respectively.

Strong LoRa Growth Boosts SMTC's Prospects

Semtech is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

SMTC's Valuation Reflects High Growth Expectations

SMTC is currently trading at a higher price-to-sales (P/S) multiple compared with the industry. SMTC's forward 12-month P/S ratio sits at 9.82X, higher than the industry's forward 12-month P/S ratio of 8.43X.

SMTC Forward 12-Month P/S Ratio

SMTC stock also trades at a higher P/S multiple compared with other industry peers, including Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors. At present, Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors have P/S multiples of 5.89X, 4.18X and 3.72X, respectively.

SMTC's rally reflects investor excitement about AI-related data center demand, putting it above industry and peers in terms of valuation, reflecting the high growth expectations of the company in the long term.

Conclusion: Buy SMTC Stock Right Now

Semtech is seeing strong demand for AI data center products, with the ramp-up of 1.6T solutions driving revenue growth and a strong backlog supporting future demand. news.Title: ASML vs. SIMO: Which Chip Stock Has More Growth Potential Today?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML and Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO are two premier semiconductor firms focusing on advanced chip technologies and the broader semiconductor ecosystem. Both players are well-positioned to gain from growing demand for advanced computing, with ASML supplying the lithography equipment essential for manufacturing semiconductors and SIMO developing NAND flash controllers for SSDs and data storage applications.

ASML provides sophisticated hardware, software and systems that enable semiconductor manufacturers to produce increasingly smaller, faster and more energy-efficient chips. Its technologies are primarily used in the lithography stage of semiconductor manufacturing, in which complex circuit patterns are transferred onto silicon wafers.

Silicon Motion is a leading developer of microcontroller ICs for NAND flash storage devices. The semiconductor firm also designs, develops and markets high-performance, low-power semiconductor solutions for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and other customers.

Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

The Case for ASML

Rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is one of ASML's most powerful growth catalysts. Training and inference workloads require increasingly powerful and energy-efficient processors, which are accelerating the transition toward smaller process nodes and more advanced memory technologies. The ongoing investments and continued progress in AI technologies are further boosting demand for both advanced Logic and Memory chips. Semiconductor manufacturers are accelerating capacity expansion plans, resulting in stronger commitments across ASML's product portfolio.

ASML's decision to materially increase manufacturing capacity provides another indication of strengthening demand visibility. Based on strong customer commitments, the company plans to increase its 2027 Low-NA EUV capacity by approximately 30% from its 2026 capacity of roughly 65 systems. It is also evaluating another roughly 30% capacity increase for 2028. A similar expansion is underway for immersion DUV. ASML plans to raise capacity by around 30% in 2027 from a 2026 level of roughly 130 systems and is evaluating another 30% increase for 2028. Capacity expansion suggests that customers are providing ASML with higher visibility into their multi-year fab and technology plans.

However, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. Although this has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, it makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing, resulting in elevated operational risks.

Story Continues

The Case for SIMO

Silicon Motion has established itself as the leading merchant supplier of client SSD (solid state drive) controllers to module makers, including most market leaders in the United States, Taiwan and China. The company believes that it is well-equipped to adapt to industry changes as it has collaborated with flash vendors to develop proprietary controller technology to overcome the existing weakness of 3D NAND and outshine peers. Silicon Motion has commenced initial sales of 3D SSD controllers to flash partners. It expects this controller to be a significant SSD controller growth driver for the next year, as NAND Flash partners' 3D capacity expands.

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not need expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This, in turn, enables the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity. The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. Over the past 10 years, the company has shipped more than 5 billion controllers cumulatively – more than any other company in the world. Silicon Motion ships more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

However, sluggishness in the global economy is likely to weigh on the company's wireless and broader semiconductor market. The demand for PCs and smartphones in the end market continues to be soft as numerous suppliers are focusing on reducing their inventory levels. The near-term price fluctuation in the PC market remains a concern. Silicon Motion continues to acquire a large number of companies. While this improves revenue opportunities, business mix and profitability, it adds to integration risks. Moreover, the semiconductor industry is highly dynamic as it is prone to swift technological changes, stiff competition from evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for ASML & SIMO?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ASML's 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 35.4%, while that for EPS indicates a surge of 56.9%. The EPS estimates have trended up 2.2% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SIMO's 2026 sales indicates a year-over-year growth of 112.9%, while that for EPS suggests a rise of 214.4%. The EPS estimates have remained static over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of ASML & SIMO

Over the past year, Silicon Motion has soared 194% compared with the industry's growth of 159.6%. ASML has gained 80.8% over the same period.

Silicon Motion looks more attractive than ASML from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, ASML's shares currently trade at 11.79 forward sales, higher than 3.77 for SIMO.

ASML or SIMO: Which is a Better Pick?

ASML currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), while SIMO carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

With a superior Zacks Rank and better fundamentals, Silicon Motion appears to be relatively better placed than ASML. Consequently, SIMO is a better investment option at the moment.
